The Right Roofing Decision Is Not Always Replacement

class=”rr-k12-tab is-active” type=”button” role=”tab” aria-selected=”true” aria-controls=”rr-maintain” id=”rr-maintain-tab” data-target=”rr-maintain”> Maintain class=”rr-k12-tab” type=”button” role=”tab” aria-selected=”false” aria-controls=”rr-repair” id=”rr-repair-tab” data-target=”rr-repair”> Repair class=”rr-k12-tab” type=”button” role=”tab” aria-selected=”false” aria-controls=”rr-replace” id=”rr-replace-tab” data-target=”rr-replace”> Replace

MAINTAIN CONTENT ========================== –> class=”rr-k12-panel is-active” id=”rr-maintain” role=”tabpanel” aria-labelledby=”rr-maintain-tab”>

REPLACE THIS IMAGE URL –> src=”https://rhodenroofing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Maintenance-Screenshot-Two-Workers-Magd-scaled.png” alt=”Roof maintenance example” class=”rr-k12-image”>

Preserve what is worth preserving.

When a roof has years of service life remaining, preventive maintenance helps preserve its remaining useful life and keep your district’s replacement timeline intact. Regular maintenance is the most cost-effective way to extend the life of a roof, which is why many manufacturing warranties require bi-annual inspections for warranty coverage. We document all inspection findings and maintenance items in a record that is accessible for your district. class=”rr-k12-panel-link” href=”https://rhodenroofing.com/commercial-roof-maintenance/”> Explore RoofCare →

REPAIR CONTENT ========================== –> class=”rr-k12-panel” id=”rr-repair” role=”tabpanel” aria-labelledby=”rr-repair-tab” hidden>

REPLACE THIS IMAGE URL –> src=”https://rhodenroofing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/down-net_http20260903-140-y9sktp.jpg” alt=”Commercial roof repair example” class=”rr-k12-image”>

Address the problem without replacing the roof.

When repairs remain a responsible use of capital, we identify the affected areas, define the corrective work, and help the district preserve a roof that still has useful service life remaining. Invasive repairs require the removal and replacement of items on the roof. The earlier these vulnerabilities are found, the less opportunity water has to saturate insulation and cause interior damage, which increases repair costs. class=”rr-k12-panel-link” href=”https://rhodenroofing.com/commercial-roofing-wichita/”> Explore Our Commercial Roofing Services →

REPLACE CONTENT ========================== –> class=”rr-k12-panel” id=”rr-replace” role=”tabpanel” aria-labelledby=”rr-replace-tab” hidden>

REPLACE THIS IMAGE URL –> src=”https://rhodenroofing.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Crane-Lowered-Material-Workers-with-HVAC-Replacement-1.jpg” alt=”Roof replacement with crew and crane” class=”rr-k12-image”>

Replace within the plan.

When maintenance and repairs are no longer a responsible use of district capital, we help define the replacement scope, timing, and roofing system around the district’s long-term plan. Our job is not to sell you a roof. As district partners, our job is to help districts make the right decision. When it is time for replacement, we stand behind our work for the lifetime of your roof. class=”rr-k12-panel-link” href=”https://rhodenroofing.com/commercial-roofing-wichita/”> Explore Roof Replacement Options →

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” background_color=”#ffffff” custom_margin=”|1vw||1vw|false|true” custom_padding=”1.2vw|1.5vw|1.2vw|1.5vw|true|true” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Why FiberTite for Schools?

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” text_text_color=”#223311″ text_letter_spacing=”0.5px” header_2_text_color=”#223311″ custom_margin=”||0px||false|false” custom_padding=”|20px|0px|20px|false|true” custom_css_free_form=”.vertical-align {||display: flex;||flex-direction: column;||justify-content: center;||}||” global_colors_info=”{}”]

FiberTite roof systems are built around a KEE-based membrane with heavy reinforcement and a four-layer construction designed to resist punctures, UV exposure, chemicals, and ponding water. Its ASTM-verified Environmental Product Declaration uses a 40-year reference service life, giving districts a longer planning horizon when replacement is the responsible next step.

For a district, longer service life is not just a roofing benefit. Fewer replacement cycles mean fewer major capital events, less disruption, and a lower total cost of ownership over time.

Rhoden Roofing is an independent installer not affiliated with FiberTite nor any individual manufacturer. We consult on the best roof system for your district.

title=”What is the best time of the year to replace a school’s roof? ” open=”on” open_toggle_text_color=”#000000″ closed_toggle_text_color=”#e6e7e8″ closed_toggle_background_color=”#2d2c39″ _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”20px||12px||false|false” custom_padding=”20px||20px||true|false” border_color_bottom=”#ca2026″ border_width_bottom_last_edited=”off|desktop” global_colors_info=”{}” border_width_bottom__hover_enabled=”on|hover” border_width_bottom__hover=”2.5px”]

For most schools, summer break is the best time to replace a roof because it reduces conflict with classes, student traffic and any occupied spaces. However, roof work can be completed at other times, such as fall or spring break, so an actively leaking or failing roof should not simply be left until summer. 

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”How often should a school district inspect its roofs?” open_toggle_text_color=”#000000″ closed_toggle_text_color=”#e6e7e8″ closed_toggle_background_color=”#2d2c39″ _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”20px||12px||false|false” custom_padding=”20px||20px||true|false” border_color_bottom=”#ca2026″ border_width_bottom_last_edited=”off|desktop” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_line_height=”1.5em” border_width_bottom__hover=”2.5px” border_width_bottom__hover_enabled=”on|hover” open=”off”]

A school roof should be inspected at least twice a year, typically in the spring and fall, and after major storms. Regular inspections help identify vulnerabilities before they cause interior leaks or damage. For schools, maintaining consistent inspection records also gives districts better information for maintenance and long-term capital planning. 

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”What determines whether a school roof can be repaired or needs replacement?” open_toggle_text_color=”#000000″ closed_toggle_text_color=”#e6e7e8″ closed_toggle_background_color=”#2d2c39″ _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”20px||12px||false|false” custom_padding=”20px||20px||true|false” border_color_bottom=”#ca2026″ border_width_bottom_last_edited=”off|desktop” global_colors_info=”{}” border_width_bottom__hover=”2.5px” border_width_bottom__hover_enabled=”on|hover” open=”off”]

A school roof can often be repaired when the damage is isolated and the surrounding roof system, insulation, and deck remain dry and serviceable. Replacement, or a layover, is necessary when leaks are recurring, moisture has spread beneath the membrane, or continued repairs are simply more costly than a full replacement. 

The decision to replace a roof is not determined by its age alone, but by its documented condition and the district’s capacity to replace the roof. 

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”Can a school district replace its roofs in phases? ” open_toggle_text_color=”#000000″ closed_toggle_text_color=”#e6e7e8″ closed_toggle_background_color=”#2d2c39″ _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”20px||12px||false|false” custom_padding=”20px||20px||true|false” border_color_bottom=”#ca2026″ border_width_bottom_last_edited=”off|desktop” global_colors_info=”{}” border_width_bottom__hover=”2.5px” border_width_bottom__hover_enabled=”on|hover” open=”off”]

Yes. Large campuses often phase roof replacements by building or by roof section across multiple summers or budget cycles. High priority, vulnerable roof sections are replaced first, while other roof sections are maintained in the meantime. Rhoden Roofing has completed a K-8 roof replacement in three phases over three summers to spread both the capital expense and disruption. Consistent condition records make it easier to establish which roofs are the priority and update priorities over time. 

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”Why does Rhoden Roofing often recommend FiberTite instead of TPO or PVC for schools?” open_toggle_text_color=”#000000″ closed_toggle_text_color=”#e6e7e8″ closed_toggle_background_color=”#2d2c39″ _builder_version=”4.27.8″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”20px||40px||false|false” custom_padding=”20px||20px||true|false” border_color_bottom=”#ca2026″ border_width_bottom_last_edited=”off|desktop” global_colors_info=”{}” border_width_bottom__hover=”2.5px” border_width_bottom__hover_enabled=”on|hover” open=”off”]

A maintained FiberTite is capable of doubling the service life of a maintained TPO or PVC roof in Kansas and Oklahoma. Schools, which typically use bonds or budgeted capital expenditures to fund roofing projects, FiberTite’s longevity reduces a district’s total cost of ownership by up to 50 percent.

TPO ROOFING

What is TPO?

 

TPO is a white single-ply membrane used on low-slope roofs to create a waterproof surface. Its heat-welded seams, reflective surface and installation flexibility make it one of the most common commercial roof systems in the Midwest.

Not sure which roof covering is best for your property? We can inspect your existing roof system and outline the viability of TPO on your roof.

Schedule a Commercial Roof Assessment

When TPO Makes Sense

TPO has become popular in the lower Midwest due to its reflectiveness, repairability, and installation flexibility. It is not the solution for every building, but it is often our go-to low-slope roof covering for commercial buildings. 



Large Low-Slope Roofs

TPO is commonly used on large commercial roofs because wide membrane sheets and the option to mechanically attach make it economical at scale.



Energy-Efficient Surface

Its white surface reflects sunlight for years after installation, making it a common choice for building owners pursuing reduced energy costs.



Aging EPDM Roofs

TPO is often recommended when replacing an older rubber roof nearing the end of its service life.



Replacement or Recovery

TPO may be used when fully replacing or recovering a roof, but existing moisture and roof layers determine which solutions are possible.

TPO ROOFING

How We Evaluate a TPO Roof

 

Before recommending TPO or any repairs, we evaluate the system as a whole, the building’s use, and whether repair, replacement, or a hybrid approach will work best. 

Address the Existing Roof System

We identify your existing roof system and diagnose any active leaks you may have.

TPO is not a one-size-fits-all solution. We make sure that TPO will meet your building’s needs.

Design a Scope for Your Building

Our scope is designed to fix the problem, align with your needs and meet manufacturer spec.

Low-Slope Membrane Comparison

TPO vs. PVC vs. EPDM

 

EPDM

A rubber membrane still found on many commercial roofs in the lower Midwest.

  • Dark membrane surface
  • Flexible material
  • Often replaced with TPO at the end of its service life

 

TPO

A versatile membrane that performs well on most low-slope roofs.

  • Highly reflective white surface
  • Heat-welded seams
  • Used as a retrofit material over many existing roof systems

 

PVC

Often the better fit when the building exhausts grease or chemicals.

  • Chemically resistant
  • Heat-welded seams
  • Common on restaurants, industrial and manufacturing buildings

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

How much does a TPO roof cost?

A standard 10′ x 100′ roll of 60-mil TPO costs about $1,000, not including labor. However, a TPO roof system includes the full roof assembly, including insulation, cover board, attachment method, metals and roof access — much more than just the membrane. Most TPO roof systems cost between $8 and $18 per square foot as a result. The more complicated the roof is, the more expensive the project will be. A roof with dozens of roof-mounted HVAC units, pipes and skylights will cost more to replace than an equal-sized roof with no penetrations.

How long does a TPO roof last?

According to the NRCA, the average unmaintained low-slope roof has a service life of 10-14 years. A maintained roof often lasts nearly twice as long. In our experience, a properly installed TPO roofs can last up to 25-30 years when minor issues like small membrane tears and deteriorated sealant are addressed before they result in leaks. 

Can a TPO roof be installed over an existing roof?

Yes, and it’s commonly done on roofs that are relatively healthy as they near the end of their service life. Also known as a layover, installing TPO over an existing roof eliminates the operational disruption and cost associated with tearing off the existing roof. There are two prerequisites for a layover. 

  1. No more than one existing roof layer.
  2. Healthy, dry substrate. 

If your roof meets those conditions, it may be eligible for a layover. 

For more information, we compare a layover against a complete replacement in our article Layover vs Remove-and-Replace On a Membrane Roof: When Does it Make Sense?

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

How do I know if my roof has hail damage?

Hail-damaged roofs often look fine from the ground, but here are four warning signs to look for without mounting your roof:

  1. Granules collecting in gutters or beneath downspouts.
  2. Dents on gutters, downspouts, or garage doors.
  3. Neighbors receiving roof replacements after a storm.
  4. Roofing companies canvassing your neighborhood after a storm.

These signs do not guarantee a successful insurance claim, but they justify a closer look. The most reliable way to know is a professional roof inspection with photo documentation.

How long do I have to file an insurance claim on my roof?

Many homeowners’ policies allow one year from the date of loss, while some allow two years or more — claim deadlines vary by carrier and policy. 

The best way to know for sure is to contact your insurance carrier or agent and ask about your policy. If your roof was affected by a recent storm, it is smart to act sooner rather than later. 

Can roofing contractors waive my insurance deductible?

No, waiving the insurance deductible constitutes insurance fraud.

If a contractor promises to “cover your deductible,” ask questions and review the agreement carefully. Reputable contractors focus on quality workmanship, clear pricing, and helping you understand the claims process, not commit insurance fraud.

We explain how contractors try to commit insurance fraud in our article Is it Legal for Roofing Companies to Waive Insurance Deductibles?

From inspection to construction, how long does it take to complete a roof?

Most roofing projects take between three weeks and four months, depending on weather, material availability, and seasonal demand. 

When the weather is calm and temperatures are 40 degrees and rising, we install between 20-25 roofs per week. After a hailstorm, schedules often extend because many homeowners need help at the same time. 

We keep customers informed throughout the process so expectations are clear from the beginning. To learn what happens behind the scenes after a roofing contract is signed, see our article What Happens After You Sign a Roofing Contract? A Behind-the-Scenes Guide. 

Why should I trust Rhoden Roofing with my insurance claim?

Rhoden Roofing has an in-house insurance claims team that helps you navigate the claims process. Our goal with every project is to eliminate confusion, protect your interests and property, and build a roof that lasts a lifetime.

Will insurance cover my roof replacement in Kansas?

If your roof was damaged by a covered event such as hail, homeowner’s insurance may cover part or all of a roof replacement, depending on your policy terms. 

Coverage depends on the cause of damage, the age and condition of your roof, your policy, and whether insurable damage can be verified on your roof. 

The first step is a professional roof inspection with photo documentation so you can decide whether filing a claim makes sense. 

How do I lower my insurance premiums?

Insurance premiums are based on risk. Home improvements that reduce risk, like maintaining the home well, installing impact-resistant shingles, or simply installing a new roof may lower your insurance premiums. 

When replacing a roof, Kansas homeowners often ask about discounts for a new roof or Class 3 or Class 4 impact-resistant shingles, which some carriers offer significant discounts for.

Because every carrier assigns risk differently, the best way to know what will save you money is to ask your insurance agent directly.

How do I know if I need a roof replacement in Salina, KS?

A commercial roof replacement usually takes anywhere from a few days to a few weeks depending on building size, weather conditions, and system complexity. Smaller buildings may be completed quickly, while multi-building or multi-family projects require more coordination.

Commercial Roofing Service in Manhattan, KS

The Commercial Roofing Company Manhattan Property Owners Rely On

If you own a commercial building in Manhattan, your roof is not a cosmetic upgrade. It’s infrastructure.

It protects tenants near Kansas State University. It protects inventory off Tuttle Creek Boulevard. It protects operations in warehouses and retail spaces across the Little Apple. And when it fails, it becomes expensive fast.

Kansas weather is predictable in one way: it’s unpredictable. Hailstorms roll through. Wind follows. Flat roofs collect water. Insurance paperwork gets complicated. Many commercial roofing companies show up after a storm, install quickly, and disappear just as fast. Leaving business owners with commercial roofing services they can’t count on.

That’s not how we operate.

Rhoden Roofing LLC has been a top rated roofing company serving Kansas since 2008. We’re certified with major low-slope manufacturers including GAF, Mulehide, and FiberTite. We maintain an A+ BBB rating. And we back our commercial installations with a Lifetime Workmanship Warranty. That means if there’s an installation defect, we handle it. Period.

If you need a serious commercial roofing company in Manhattan that treats your building like a long-term asset, request your commercial roofing estimate today.

 

Get A FREE Estimate

Full-Service Commercial Roofing Services for Manhattan Businesses

We provide complete commercial roofing solutions designed for durability, compliance, and long-term performance in Kansas conditions.

Commercial Roof Installation

New construction or building expansion requires precision. We install low-slope and flat roofing systems according to manufacturer specifications so your roof qualifies for extended material warranties. No shortcuts. No guesswork.

Commercial Roof Repair

Not every roof needs replacement. We identify membrane punctures, flashing failures, seam separation, and storm impact damage. If a repair makes financial sense, we’ll recommend it. If it doesn’t, we’ll explain why.

Commercial Roof Replacement

When a roof reaches the end of its service life, or hail damage is extensive, replacement is often the smartest move. We remove failing systems, address insulation and drainage issues, and install complete systems eligible for up to 50-year non-prorated material warranties on qualifying products.

Roof Coatings & Restoration

For certain systems, commercial roof coatings can extend lifespan and improve reflectivity. We evaluate whether restoration is viable before recommending full replacement.

Commercial Roofing Systems We Install

Choosing the right system matters more than choosing the cheapest bid.

TPO Roofing Systems

TPO is ideal for flat and low-slope buildings throughout Manhattan. It offers strong seam performance, UV resistance, and energy efficiency.

PVC Roofing Systems

PVC systems are durable and resistant to chemicals, making them a strong fit for restaurants, industrial facilities, and commercial kitchens.

Commercial Metal Roofing

Metal roofing provides structural durability and long-term value for warehouses, agricultural buildings, and commercial facilities.

Low-Slope Roofing Systems

We install low-slope systems engineered for proper drainage and performance under Kansas wind and hail conditions.

Industries and Property Types We Serve

Commercial roofing in Manhattan requires experience across different property types. We work with:

  • Office buildings
  • Retail centers
  • Multi-family complexes
  • Industrial facilities
  • Warehouses
  • Churches and educational facilities

Multi-family and insurance-funded roof replacements are among our most requested commercial services. We coordinate projects carefully to minimize disruption for tenants and operations.

Why Choose Rhoden Roofing LLC for Commercial Roofing Services in Manhattan

You have options. Here’s what separates professionals from storm chasers:

  • Workmanship warranties that expire in 1–5 years
  • Vague contracts
  • Poor communication once the job starts
  • Installations that don’t meet manufacturer requirements

We do things differently.

  • Lifetime Workmanship Warranty
  • 50-year non-prorated material warranties on qualifying systems
  • Manufacturer-certified installation crews
  • Insurance claim assistance
  • A+ BBB rating
  • Serving Kansas since 2008

We don’t aim to be the cheapest. We aim to be the most reliable long-term decision you make for your building.

What We Offer Outside of Commercial Roofing Services

In addition to commercial roofing, we provide:

  • Residential roofing
  • Storm damage repair
  • Asphalt shingle systems
  • Metal, tile, slate, and cedar roofing
  • Gutter installation
  • Roof coatings

Explore All Services

Other Areas We Serve

In addition to Manhattan, we serve commercial and residential clients in: 

  • Wichita, KS
  • Andover, KS
  • Derby, KS
  • Haysville, KS
  • Goddard, KS. 

See all areas we serve to find your location.

Our Commercial Roofing Services and Installation Process

We keep the process clear so you know exactly what to expect.

Step 1: On-Site Inspection

We conduct a detailed evaluation of membrane condition, drainage performance, flashing, and storm impact. You receive documentation and straightforward recommendations.

Step 2: Written Proposal

You’ll receive a defined scope outlining system type, pricing, timeline, and warranty details. No vague language.

Step 3: Professional Installation

Our certified crews install according to manufacturer guidelines and Kansas building codes. We prioritize safety and minimize business disruption.

Step 4: Final Inspection & Warranty Registration

We complete a final walkthrough and register applicable manufacturer warranties to ensure full protection.

Request a Commercial Roofing Estimate in Manhattan, KS

If you own commercial property in Manhattan, waiting rarely makes roofing problems cheaper. A small leak becomes interior damage. Minor hail impact becomes membrane failure.

Schedule your commercial roofing inspection with Rhoden Roofing LLC today. We’ll evaluate your roof, explain your options clearly, and help you make a smart, long-term decision.

If you live in Manhattan and you’re tired of worrying about your roof, schedule your inspection with Rhoden Roofing today. We’ll make this the last roof you ever have to think about.

Call 316-927-2233 today to request your estimate and speak directly with a commercial roofing company that understands Kansas weather, commercial systems, and insurance requirements.

FAQs About Commercial Roofing Services in Manhattan, KS

Before you move forward with a repair or replacement, you should have clear answers. As a trusted commercial roofing company providing services in Manhattan, here are the most common questions we hear from commercial property owners—and the straight answers.

How long does a commercial roof last in Manhattan, KS?

A commercial roof in Manhattan, KS typically lasts 20 to 40 years depending on the system, installation quality, and maintenance history. TPO, PVC, and metal systems perform well when installed by an experienced commercial roofing company and supported with routine commercial roofing service inspections after major hail or wind events. Kansas weather plays a major role in lifespan.

Should I repair or replace my commercial roof?

Whether you should repair or replace your commercial roof depends on its age and extent of damage. Minor membrane issues or isolated leaks can often be repaired, but widespread hail damage or recurring leaks usually make replacement the more cost-effective long-term decision.

How do I know if my commercial roof has hail damage?

You know your commercial roof has hail damage when there are visible membrane punctures, seam separation, flashing dents, or documented impact marks. The most reliable way to confirm damage is through a professional inspection with photo documentation for insurance.

Do you help with commercial roofing insurance claims?

title.rendered: The Gift of Community: Janet Brown’s Inspiring Roof Giveaway Story

content.rendered:
The Gift of Community: Janet Brown’s Inspiring Roof Giveaway Story

EL DORADO, Kan. — When Janet Brown’s aging roof became a problem, she feared losing the home she shared with her brother, who had muscular dystrophy and dementia.

“I was so scared,” Brown said. “I knew my roof wasn’t going to make it, and I was scared that he was going to have to move someplace else.”

Everything changed in 2009, when Brown became the inaugural recipient of a free roof from the Roof Giveaway. The Roof Giveaway is a program created by Rhoden Roofing in 2009 to support deserving families in need. Her story became the starting point for an initiative that has since helped 18 families across the Wichita area.

A Life-Changing Phone Call

A dozen friends and family members nominated Brown for the Roof Giveaway, inspired by her selflessness and devotion to others. Brown, who was subsidizing home health care to keep her brother at home, didn’t nominate herself. Even as she supported her brother with home health care, she continued giving back, volunteering at the Wichita Children’s Home. When she received the call notifying her that she had been selected, Brown was on her way to volunteer.

“All I could do was cry,” she said. “For the first month [after installation], every time I came home, I just got teary-eyed. And I still do.”

The new roof brought immediate relief, allowing her to focus on caring for her brother without the looming worry of a state inspection or additional damage.

Built on Friendship

Brown’s home has always represented community. Built by her then-husband and his Navy friends in 1982, the house quickly became a hub of activity for neighbors and family.

“This house was built on friendship, pure and simple,” Brown said. “It’s full of love.”

That spirit lives on every December. Brown decorates her home with a Christmas display that draws visitors from across the area. Children gather on her and her husband Wayne’s lawn to take photos with Santa, while neighbors visit to admire her Christmas tree and village.

“It’s no Christmas Vacation, but it’s peaceful out here,” she said.

A Ripple Effect of Kindness

When Rhoden Roofing’s team arrived to install her new roof, Brown couldn’t help but give back in her own way. Greeting the crew with homemade cinnamon rolls, burgers, chicken, and boxed meals, she ensured no one left her home empty-handed.

Brown turned her gratitude for the free roof into an opportunity to give back. When Rhoden Roofing’s team arrived to replace her roof, she greeted them with homemade cinnamon rolls, burgers, and boxed meals.

“There was so much food,” she said, laughing. “I had to send them off with plates. They joked they needed a siesta before starting their next job.”

This kind of mutual kindness is what makes the Roof Giveaway unique. When families aren’t worried about the roof over their heads, they have the stability they need to make a difference in their communities. Brown is gracious and kind, and helping people like her in times of need is the ultimate privilege for Rhoden Roofing.

“It’s okay to ask for help,” Brown said. “It’s 15 years later and I wouldn’t be here without that roof.”

Applications Now Open

Last year, the Roof Giveaway provided free roofs to two deserving families in the Wichita area. Applicants are encouraged to tell their stories, or the story of their nominee.

Applications for the 2024 Rhoden Roofing Roof Giveaway are open through Jan. 12, 2025. The recipient will be announced on Feb. 14, 2025. To learn more or nominate someone in need, apply here on our website or call (316) 927-2233 with any questions about the application process.

Apply Now

Andover’s Trusted Metal Roofing Company

Your Leading Metal Roofing Contractor Serving Andover

Metal roofs have many distinct advantages over other roofing materials. They are durable, lightweight, easy to install, and fireproof. With a wide variety of colors and styles to choose from, Rhoden Roofing can achieve virtually any look you want for your home.
Get A FREE Estimate

Types of Metal Roofing

Metal roofing offers a wide spectrum of variations and materials under its umbrella, all of which can be installed by Rhoden Roofing out of Andover, KS. These are some of the most popular metal roofing varieties:

Aluminium Roofing

Aluminium roofing has many benefits that homeowners and business owners are attracted to. While it is durable, corrosion-resistant, cost-effective, and eco-friendly, aluminum roofing also doesn’t rust, enables smoother water runoff, and reflects the sun better than other metal roofing materials. This also makes it energy-efficient.

Steel Roofing

A popular choice for roofing in hail-prone areas particularly, steel roofing is super durable and low maintenance, which ranks it high on the longevity scale. Like most metal roofing materials, the heat reflection also contributes to reduced energy use and costs.

Copper Roofing

Copper as a roofing material is definitely one of the rare metal roofing alternatives, but its unique finish is one of its stand-out features and one that is bound to increase the home’s curb appeal. Given its lightweight and malleability, it can be fashioned in a variety of ways to mimic tiles, shingles, brick, etc.

Standing Seam Metal Roofing

Standing-seam roofs are the most popular iteration of metal roofing. Essentially, this type of roofing raises the seams beyond the level of the actual roof, thereby creating panels that run from the ridge to the eaves of the roof. Its interlocking system ensures that a watertight seal is created, and also makes it one of the strongest, most reliable roof systems on the market today.

Corrugated Metal Roofing

Corrugated metal is made from galvanized steel rolled into a wavy pattern. This corrugation process enhances the strength of the material, making corrugated metal roofing a tough metal roofing option. It’s often seen in the industry and less on homes, but its lightweight, durability, and water-shedding features are making it a viable option for the home.

Metal Shingles

Metal shingles are one of the most popular options for residential roofing. Its major appeal is the combination of all the great characteristics of metal while giving homeowners the ability to customize the look and feel to their preference. Metal shingles can mimic the finish of more premium roofing alternatives like slate roofs, clay and concrete tiles, and cedar, at a fraction of the cost, and with strength, durability, and longevity guaranteed.

Costs

For a lot more detail and a breakdown of roofing costs to expect for replacements, repairs, and components, see our Cost Series.

Advantages of Metal Roofs

Metal is one of the most reliable roofing materials on the market for both residential and commercial roofs. These are some of the characteristics that make it a great roofing option:

Durability

Metal roofing holds up well against all types of harsh weather conditions. It is even able to withstand debris and animal activity. The impact of extreme weather in the Andover area makes metal roofing an excellent choice for durability.

Low maintenance

Maintenance on a metal roof is so easy that you could almost install it and forget about it. As with any roofing material, regular maintenance is a must, but the upkeep on metal roofing is so limited, that compared to other solutions like shingles, concrete, or tile, you’ll have a worry-free roof and save on costs in the long run.

Longevity

Its durability and ease of maintenance contribute to metal roofing lasting a very long time – up to 50-70 years. That means that you may very well never have to replace your home’s roof again in your lifetime.

Environmentally friendly

In most cases, a quality metal roof will be made of anything from 35% – 95% recyclable and/or recycled material. While the lifespan of a metal roofing will be very long, when it does come time to remove it for whatever reason, the entire thing will be 100% recyclable, as opposed to being dumped in a landfill. In addition, its heat-reflecting capabilities mean the homeowner will save on home energy costs too, by reducing the need for cooling in the home.

Value

While your metal roofing will cost more upfront to install, it will cost less over its lifetime. The long-term investment is well worth it considering the reduction of maintenance and repair costs over the roof’s lifetime – a far cry from alternatives like asphalt shingles. On top of that, metal roof warranties also tend to be exceptional.

Get A FREE Estimate

The Pros and Cons of Asphalt Shingle Roofing

When making your decision about the type of roofing you prefer, there will be pros and cons. It’s best to know what to expect. 

Pros of Asphalt Shingles

  • Affordability: in conjunction with financing options, asphalt is a no-brainer for homeowners on a budget. With proper installation and maintenance, a quality roof doesn’t have to break the bank.
  • Color Variety: It comes in a wide variety of colors, ranging from neutrals to statement colors. Depending on how much you want to spend, you can even choose asphalt shingle roofing that emulates wood or slate.
  • Simple Installation: Asphalt shingle roof repair is simple and cost-effective. New shingles can sometimes be installed on top of existing shingles. With proper maintenance asphalt shingle roofing has a lifespan of up to 20 years.

Cons of Asphalt Shingles

  • Not Environmentally Friendly: Asphalt shingles are not recyclable since they can release harmful emissions. As the shortest roof lifespan, asphalt shingles contribute a lot of waste.
  • Susceptible to Weather: Wide-ranging temperatures and extreme weather conditions can cause cracks and warping of some asphalt shingle types.

FAQs

How long do metal roofs last?

Metal is one of the roofing materials giving homeowners minimal hassle and bang for their buck in terms of longevity. While some materials may require a roof replacement every 20-30 years, metal roofs can enjoy a lifespan of 40-70 years. This means you may never have to replace your home’s roof in your lifetime again.

Are metal roofs noisy when it rains?
Many have this misconception of noise is caused by metal roofing, thanks in large part due to older methods of installation. These days metal roofs are installed over the solid roof deck, which, apart from providing a foundation, also functions to absorb sound. This greatly reduces noise caused by rain or hail and what you hear is likely at the same pitch as other roofing material types.
Do metal roofs keep the house cooler?

One of metal’s best characteristics is the fact that it reflects heat in summer, which can greatly reduce the home’s temperature and mitigate the need for any energy-guzzling artificial cooling.

Eastborough’s Trusted Metal Roofing Company

Your Leading Metal Roofing Contractor Serving Eastborough

Metal roofs have many distinct advantages over other roofing materials. They are durable, lightweight, easy to install, and fireproof. With a wide variety of colors and styles to choose from, Rhoden Roofing can achieve virtually any look you want for your home.

Get A FREE Estimate

Types of Metal Roofing

Metal roofing offers a wide spectrum of variations and materials under its umbrella, all of which can be installed by Rhoden Roofing out of Eastborough, KS. These are some of the most popular metal roofing varieties:

Aluminium Roofing

Aluminium roofing has many benefits that homeowners and business owners are attracted to. While it is durable, corrosion-resistant, cost-effective, and eco-friendly, aluminum roofing also doesn’t rust, enables smoother water runoff, and reflects the sun better than other metal roofing materials. This also makes it energy-efficient.

Steel Roofing

A popular choice for roofing in hail-prone areas particularly, steel roofing is super durable and low maintenance, which ranks it high on the longevity scale. Like most metal roofing materials, the heat reflection also contributes to reduced energy use and costs.

Copper Roofing

Copper as a roofing material is definitely one of the rare metal roofing alternatives, but its unique finish is one of its stand-out features and one that is bound to increase the home’s curb appeal. Given its lightweight and malleability, it can be fashioned in various ways to mimic tiles, shingles, brick, etc.

Standing Seam Metal Roofing

Standing-seam roofs are the most popular iteration of metal roofing. Essentially, this type of roofing raises the seams beyond the level of the actual roof, thereby creating panels that run from the ridge to the roof’s eaves. Its interlocking system ensures that a watertight seal is created, making it one of the strongest, most reliable roof systems on the market today.

Corrugated Metal Roofing

Corrugated metal is made from galvanized steel rolled into a wavy pattern. This corrugation process enhances the strength of the material, making corrugated metal roofing a tough metal roofing option. It’s often seen in the industry and less on homes, but its lightweight, durability, and water-shedding features are making it a viable option for the home.

Metal Shingles

Metal shingles are one of the most popular options for residential roofing. Its major appeal is the combination of all the great characteristics of metal while giving homeowners the ability to customize the look and feel to their preference. Metal shingles can mimic the finish of more premium roofing alternatives like slate roofs, clay and concrete tiles, and cedar, at a fraction of the cost, and with strength, durability, and longevity guaranteed.

Get A FREE Estimate

Costs

For a lot more detail and a breakdown of roofing costs to expect for replacements, repairs, and components, see our Cost Series.

Advantages of Metal Roofs

Metal is one of the most reliable roofing materials on the market for both residential and commercial roofs. These are some of the characteristics that make it a great roofing option:

Durability

Metal roofing holds up well against all types of harsh weather conditions. It is even able to withstand debris and animal activity. The impact of extreme weather in the Eastborough area makes metal roofing an excellent choice for durability.

Low maintenance

Maintenance on a metal roof is so easy that you could almost install it and forget about it. As with any roofing material, regular maintenance is a must, but the upkeep on metal roofing is so limited, that compared to other solutions like shingles, concrete, or tile, you’ll have a worry-free roof and save on costs in the long run.

Longevity

Its durability and ease of maintenance contribute to metal roofing lasting a very long time – up to 50-70 years. That means that you may very well never have to replace your home’s roof again in your lifetime.

Environmentally friendly

In most cases, a quality metal roof will be made of anything from 35% – 95% recyclable and/or recycled material. While the lifespan of a metal roofing will be very long, when it does come time to remove it for whatever reason, the entire thing will be 100% recyclable, as opposed to being dumped in a landfill. In addition, its heat-reflecting capabilities mean the homeowner will save on home energy costs too, by reducing the need for cooling in the home.

Value

While your metal roofing will cost more upfront to install, it will cost less over its lifetime. The long-term investment is well worth it considering the reduction of maintenance and repair costs over the roof’s lifetime – a far cry from alternatives like asphalt shingles. On top of that, metal roof warranties also tend to be exceptional.

Metal Roofing FAQs

How long do metal roofs last?
Metal is one of the roofing materials giving homeowners minimal hassle and bang for their buck in terms of longevity. While some materials may require a roof replacement every 20-30 years, metal roofs can enjoy a lifespan of 40-70 years. This means you may never have to replace your home’s roof in your lifetime.
Are metal roofs noisy when it rains?

Many have this misconception of noise is caused by metal roofing, thanks in large part due to older methods of installation. These days metal roofs are installed over the solid roof deck, which, apart from providing a foundation, also functions to absorb sound. This greatly reduces noise caused by rain or hail and what you hear is likely at the same pitch as other roofing material types.

Do metal roofs keep the house cooler?
One of metal’s best characteristics is the fact that it reflects heat in summer, which can greatly reduce the home’s temperature and mitigate the need for any energy-guzzling artificial cooling.

Habitat for Humanity

Our Mission

 

We care about supporting and giving back to our community. We work closely with Wichita Habitat for Humanity in order to bring safe and affordable housing to those who need it most. In 2019, we completed two Habitat for Humanity roofs. Then in 2020 our team at Rhoden Roofing donated and orchestrated the installation of six of the eight homes built by the Wichita Habitat for Humanity.

But in 2021, we wanted to do more. Wichita Habitat for Humanity set the goal of 20 roofs in 2021, and we knew that we could reach this goal with the help of other GAF Master Elite contractors in the area. So with the help of GAF supplying the materials, we reached out and coordinated with other local contractors. With everyone chipping in, the 20 roofing projects are already scheduled to be completed this year with absolutely no cost to the homeowners. The greater Wichita area serves us so well, and we feel we have the responsibility to give back to those who may not have the means.

We intend on continuing our partnership with GAF and Wichita Habitat for Humanity as we remain dedicated to help more families in this community. To learn more about our work with Wichita Habitat for Humanity in 2020 check out the recommendation letter below from their Executive Director, Ann M. Fox. To learn more about our coordination with GAF’s Habitat for Humanity Contractor program to meet our goals in 2021 see this blog post from GAF.

How You Fit

We take pride in our products, our warranties and our work. But our people are what makes Rhoden Roofing Wichita’s most trusted roofing company.

We trust our team, and it’s important that our team has trust in each other. Without transparency, this isn’t possible. To achieve transparency, we answer questions, not escalate them.

Have questions of your own? Connect with us directly at (316) 927-2233.

Our Teams

Project Coordination

Project Coordinators are the customer’s trusted partner. They design custom roof systems, address challenges proactively, and bring their vision to life. It’s about relationships, expertise, and delivering excellence.

The expert customers remember and the partner that earned their trust.

Marketing

Marketing’s job is to connect people to Rhoden Roofing—sharing our story, showcasing our work, and ensuring we’re not strangers when we meet. It’s about crafting messages that inspire, inform, and echo the excitement we have.

We make sure they know us before they meet us.

Claims

Our Claims team is the bridge between customers and their insurers, simplifying the process and securing what customers are owed. They’re expert guides in a system that often feels overwhelming.

Advocates for every claim, partners at every step.

Production

Roof replacements and repairs can be construction projects with many moving parts. Our production team brings it all together by efficiently managing time, resources, and communication with precision.

Fulfilling our promise of a roof that lasts a lifetime.

Operations

Operations works behind the scenes to ensure everything runs smoothly, identifying inefficiencies both internally and externally. They provide seamless support, enabling teams to focus on delivering exceptional results.

Turning small actions into big impacts.

WHAT SETS US APART

What sets every company apart is its people. What matters isn’t what sets a company apart; it’s how does a company treat the people that set it apart.

Beat the Budget

At Rhoden Roofing, we promise our customers a roof built to last a lifetime. To our employees, we promise this: excellence will always be recognized and rewarded.

Our Beat the Budget bonus structure is a revenue-sharing program that ensures outstanding performance benefits everyone. While the end of a quarter might be business as usual elsewhere, at Rhoden Roofing, it’s an opportunity to celebrate company-wide achievement and reward the hard work that made it possible.

EOS

Too often, meetings feel like a formality—scheduled, attended, and quickly forgotten. At Rhoden Roofing, we’ve embraced the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS) to ensure every meeting serves a purpose.

Using EOS’ L10 framework, we set clear quarterly goals, or “rocks,” and track progress in weekly meetings. If a meeting misses the mark, participants rate it, and we adjust to stay on course. This approach ensures every voice is heard, every issue is addressed, and everyone knows what they’re working toward. The result is meetings that drive action and deliver clarity, not confusion.

Complete Ownership

Hanging a photo in a rental property means worrying about patching the wall before your lease is up. Hanging a photo in a home you own is different—your only concern is making it fit, making it yours.

At Rhoden Roofing, we believe your work should belong to you. Everyone on our team takes pride in owning their work and ensuring it’s completed with care.

State of the Company

Imagine trying to solve a problem you didn’t know existed—it’s impossible. The same is true for a company. That’s why at Rhoden Roofing, we share everything: our challenges, successes, and plans for the future. For example, every quarter you review your supervisor in one-on-ones designed to find your paths to career growth with Rhoden Roofing.

Our State of the Company meetings ensure everyone knows where we stand and where we’re headed. No backroom discussions, no trickle-down updates—just facts, shared openly with the entire team.

Competitive Benefits

When your foundation is secure, you can focus on building your future. At Rhoden Roofing, we provide the stability you need to thrive with:

  • Comprehensive health insurance, including vision and dental.
  • A 401(k) plan with company matching to help you invest in what matters most.
  • Immediate access to Paid Time Off upon hire.
  • Bonuses that reward your contributions.

Health and planning are prerequisites for success. We believe that when your needs are met, you’re free to grow, excel, and reach new heights. We’re here to support you every step of the way.

Our Core Values

Evolve and Adapt

If you are not constantly learning and improving, you are not reaching your full potential. Everyone in the company can always be improving themselves inside and outside the company. A mistake or a “loss,” should only be viewed as an opportunity to learn and grow to make yourself and the company better in the future.

Be a Great Teammate

Respect, sincerity and high expectations guide our interactions. We foster open, honest communications, embracing tough conversations and feedback to address blind spots. We lift up struggling teammates. When there is adversity we seek solutions, not excuses, which promotes team success and sustainable culture.

Get It Done

We are 100% accountable to our customers and teammates. Customers trust us to build exceptional roofing systems. We take that commitment seriously. We will do whatever is necessary to overcome obstacles & find solutions to deliver extraordinary results.

Do the Right Thing

What do you do when no one else is looking? Always put yourself in the shoes of your customer when faced with a decision, treating their property as if it were your own. Act with integrity and honesty, always choosing what’s right over what’s easy.

How We Hire

We value authenticity over perfection. Be genuine, ask thoughtful questions and engage in honest dialogue.

1: Connecting with You

Explore our roles

Our hiring process starts with a genuine desire to be a part of something bigger.

Hear back

We personally respond to every question. The best way for us to learn how you might align with our values is to learn about you.

Evaluation

Hiring is a two-way street: while we evaluate your fit for the role, you’re evaluating us. Bring questions that help you explore what it’s like to be a part of our team.

2: Our Interview Process

The interview

Some positions comprise a round-robin interview with the relevant department to help you get to know our team and to help them learn about you, while leadership or specialized roles comprise multiple interviews with team members and leaders to provide deeper insight into our culture and expectations.

The timeline

Depending on the position, the hiring timeline can vary from a few days to a few weeks. Seasonal factors may also affect the start date, especially for project coordinator roles.

The opportunity

Growth is part of our DNA, and we will align talent with opportunity.

3: Join Our Team

Meet the team

Our onboarding process is thorough and welcoming. During your first two weeks, you’ll meet with every department and leadership team member, including the owner and COO. We live our value of transparency: you’re encouraged to ask questions and receive honest answers from everyone on the team.

Set up for success

From day one, we provide the tools, training, and support needed for success. We don’t believe in “sink or swim”—we believe in setting you up to thrive. 

Contribute

The perfect background doesn’t matter to us. It’s more important that you’re genuine and ready to contribute. We’re committed to finding the right seat for the right person.

Roof Giveaway

Rhoden Roofing’s 18th Christmas Giveaway

Every Christmas, Rhoden Roofing gives back to the Wichita Community by giving away a free roof to a deserving family or individual. The Roof Giveaway is one of the most important community projects we do each year, and definitely the one we look forward to the most. The Greater Wichita community has been so good to us since we started in 2008.

We are proud to give back to our community and show our appreciation by donating a roof to a deserving family or individual. Our team is honored to be able to help these recipients protect what matters most by staying safe and dry in their own home.

The Gift of Community: Janet Brown’s Inspiring Roof Giveaway Story

Janet’s journey reflects the impact of a simple promise: to protect what matters most.

Read More

How It Works

Every Christmas (and throughout the year, see submission form below), we ask our community to help us find a deserving family or individual in need of a new roof. People here in the greater Wichita area are invited to nominate friends, relatives, neighbors, or even themselves. At the end of the nomination period, the submissions go into review, and we narrow down the field. In addition to the details of the roof/property in question, we are also looking for deserving recipients who demonstrate good character and community engagement. During the Spring, we announce our Christmas Roof Giveaway winner and are able to begin work.

You can enter by filling out the form below!

Name of the person you are nominating

*The deadline for submissions is January 11, 2027. We will read through each letter and determine the recipient by February 15, 2027. If you or whomever you are nominating are chosen, we will contact you with details on the production schedule and construction process.

Our Team

GET A FREE ESTIMATE
John Rhoden
Owner
View Profile

John got his start in the roofing business while working at ABC Supply Co, the largest distributor of roofing materials in the world, on his summers off from college at the University of San Diego. He developed his knowledge further while working as a project manager for a large Wichita roofing company. At that point, the Wichita native and East High graduate, decided to attend medical school at Creighton University. During his second year at Med school, he decided to choose a different path for himself and moved back to Wichita to start Rhoden Roofing in 2008.

John realized there was a great opportunity in the roofing industry to change the way business was done. By listening to the concerns his customers had and educating them about their project, John and his extremely capable team were able to quickly grow Rhoden Roofing into an award-winning company. He strives everyday to find a way to make the customer experience at Rhoden Roofing the best it can be. He found the best way to accomplish this was simple, listen to the customers needs and follow through every time. No Excuses!!
Ashley Rhoden
Special Projects Exec
View Profile
Ashley started with Rhoden Roofing in 2010, and through the years has worked her way through many roles around the office. She is always focused on ways to improve business processes and customer experience. Her knack for problem solving and attention to detail make her a great resource to guide customers through insurance claims.

Ashley and John were married in 2013 and have three children. Ashley balances her role as a mother and working part-time in the office, overseeing insurance claims, company accounting, business processes, and special projects. She attended both Kapaun Mt Carmel and East High before earning her degree from Wichita State University.

Dan Gray
Integrator

View Profile

Dan serves as Rhoden Roofing’s Chief Operating Officer and EOS Implementer, bringing decades of operational leadership, administrative skill and perspective to the company.

A graduate of Friends University, Dan spent more than 20 years with Wichita’s Warren Theatres, beginning his career tearing tickets and working his way into the VP of Operations and COO role. After Warren Theatres, he continued building leadership experience in the service and construction industries. Throughout his career, Dan has developed perspective on how organizations work, how they work best, and how to align the interests of the company with the interests of the customer.

Originally from Whitewater, KS, Dan believes that Rhoden Roofing’s value of Do the Right Thing is always the best path forward.

Dan has been married to his wife, Heather, for 30 years. Together, they have three children: Hunter, Tary and Braydon. They recently welcomed their first granddaughter, Evelyn, to their family. Outside of work, Dan enjoys golfing, fishing, attending sporting events, spending time with family, and watching movies. As a longtime movie buff, he appreciates a good story, though his favorite role these days maybe grandfather.

Scott Raymond
Head of Sales

View Profile

Scott graduated from Kingman High School and earned his degree from Cowley County Community College. In 2000, he entered the Automotive Collision Repair Industry. Beginning as an estimator, his attention-to-detail, affability, and willingness to learn earned him GM and Market Manager positions before joining Rhoden Roofing in 2024.

When he’s not at work, Scott enjoys spending time with his family or working on cars. He also enjoys expanding his collection of old car memorabilia and antiquing with his wife.

Joel Rodell
Head of Business Development

View Profile
Joel joined the Rhoden Roofing team in early 2025, bringing with him 20 years of experience in the commercial construction industry.
 
He first worked as a supplier before transitioning to a business development role at a leading Design-Build firm in Wichita, where he gained invaluable expertise in the field.
A dedicated advocate for the Wichita community, Joel serves on the boards of multiple nonprofit organizations. He is also actively involved at McConnell Air Force Base, where he has earned the prestigious Golden Eagle merit. His passion lies in supporting Airmen and their families, a cause that brings him great fulfillment.
 
Outside of work, Joel enjoys traveling and tending to his home, taking particular pride in maintaining what he proudly considers “the best-looking lawn in the neighborhood.”
 
Joel’s wife is a librarian in the Maize School District, and he takes great pride in his two grown children, whose academic tracks have led them into careers that closely mirror his own.
 
 
 
Brett Worrell
Project Coordinator
View Profile

Brett, a Wichita native, joined the Rhoden Roofing team in 2011. Brett attended Kapaun Mt Carmel and was an excellent soccer player. His soccer ability earned him a college scholarship in Kansas City. Brett was integral in developing and managing a local restaurant chain before joining Rhoden Roofing. Brett married his wife, Stefanie, in 2017.

Brett’s ability to problem solve and attention to detail makes him an ideal project manager. He is certified through HAAG as a Residential and Commercial inspector. HAAG engineering sets the industry standard for insurance claims on what is and what is not considered hail & wind damage. This gives him immense authority when dealing with insurance adjustors on any type of building (homes, apartments, & businesses). This authority has lead him to manage jobs all over the state of Kansas and Missouri. He understands the needs and requirements of commercial clients with large portfolios. He is certified with Xactimate, the software insurance uses to estimate projects. He has also undergone training to become proficient in attic ventilation from AirVent.
Jordan Harter
Project Coordinator
View Profile
Jordan joined the Rhoden Roofing team in 2021. He is a Wichita native, who grew up in the College Hill area. He graduated from Kapaun Mt. Carmel High school, then attended Butler County Community college, before starting a career in the Automotive Collision Repair industry; where he spent 19 years as an Estimator and General Manager. During his career in collision repair he developed a vast knowledge of the Insurance Claims Process.

He is very detail oriented and passionate about making sure that customer service and quality workmanship are the top priority on every job. Outside of the office, Jordan enjoys playing golf and spending time outdoors with his wife and three children.
Keith Ludwig
Project Coordinator
View Profile

Keith earned a degree from Iowa State University in 74’ before moving to Wichita to manage the Andersen Window Corporations wholesale distribution facilities. Keith ultimately decided to open his own lumber business and ran a very successful company for 15 years in Wichita. When Keith is not working, he loves spending time with his 4 grand children and doting upon his wife Becky.

Keith brought his vast experience and knowledge in the construction world to Rhoden Roofing in 2011. Keith is known around the office for ensuring his customers are getting properly compensated by their insurance company. For this reason, it is very common he receives hand-written notes from his customers thanking him for his efforts. He is a HAAG certified Residential Inspector. HAAG engineering sets the industry standard for insurance claims on what is and what is not considered hail & wind damage. This gives him great standing when dealing with insurance adjustors at home inspections. He is certified with Xactimate, the software insurance uses to estimate projects. He has also undergone training to become proficient in attic ventilation from AirVent.

Dave Bennett
Project Coordinator

View Profile

Dave was born and raised in Wichita, growing up in the College Hill neighborhood. He graduated from Kapaun Mt. Carmel High School and then went on to get a bachelor’s degree from Wichita State University. Starting his career with the Wichita Wings during the early 1980’s, led to an opportunity to work in sport management in Tulsa, where he remained for 30 years raising a son and daughter there, with his wife Becky. He returned to Wichita in 2016 and is glad to be back home.

Dave’s strive for knowledge and continuous perseverance has made Rhoden Roofing extremely proud to have him on our Team. Dave is a HAAG Certified Inspector. HAAG engineering sets the industry standard for insurance claims on what is and what is not considered hail and wind damage. Dave has also undergone training to become proficient in attic ventilation from AirVent Inc.

He is glad to be a part of Rhoden Roofing and working in an exciting team environment.
Patrick Mosley
Project Coordinator
View Profile
Patrick is a Wichita native who grew up in East Wichita and attended The Independent School. Patrick has a bachelors and masters degree, both in Exercise Science. He spent 13 years of his career as a personal trainer and gym owner before deciding to pivot his career in 2022 when he joined the Rhoden Roofing team. He brings passion and excellent customer service skills with him on this new endeavor.

In his free time, Patrick and his wife, Kara, are avid adventurers and outdoors people. They enjoy camping, hiking, rock climbing, and kayaking. Patrick also trains and competes in mixed martial arts.

James Telfer
Project Coordinator

View Profile
Originally from Emporia, KS., James moved to Wichita in 2010. He has a background in Sales Management and Home Inspections. James loves helping people and can usually find something in common with anyone he meets. His thoroughness and attention to detail is a hallmark in his work with clients.

In his free time, James loves spending time with his wife, Emily, at their home in rural Butler County where they have a slew of animals including a mini-potbelly pig named Lulu. They are active in the Wichita running community and enjoy “destination marathons.” James always has at least one home project he’s working on and has also served as President of his HOA for the past 2 years.

Brayden Rupp
Project Coordinator

View Profile

Originally from Hays, KS, Brayden brings a strong background in retail sales and a deep passion for the roofing and home improvement industry. He takes pride in helping homeowners protect their most significant investments, striving to make the roof purchasing process as smooth and stress-free as possible.

Sports have always played a significant role in his life, and he enjoys spending time on the golf course whenever possible. Outside of work, Brayden finds his greatest joy in spending time with his wife and their two wonderful children—a daughter and son. He cherishes every moment spent with his family.

Real Estate Account Manager

Mitchell is especially passionate about health and wellness, valuing balance and discipline both in and out of the workplace. A huge Kansas City Chiefs fan, he brings that same team spirit and energy to his professional life. He also has an eye for gold — always aiming for excellence and success in every endeavor.

Shawn chose to work for Rhoden Roofing because of the company’s strong commitment to integrity, customer care, and quality workmanship — values that align with his own.

Transitioning to the construction industry, Cody spent five years as a Project Estimator/Manager before joining Rhoden Roofing, where he excels at fostering strong customer relationships and delivering exceptional service on every project.

Ron Barry

K-12 Strategic Development

His experience working with schools, businesses, contractors, and community stakeholders enables him to help clients navigate complex roofing and exterior improvement projects with confidence.

In 2024, Ron helped lead the successful passage of a $28.5 million bond initiative—one of the largest school bond campaigns approved in Kansas that year. He also worked directly with FEMA, EMC Insurance, contractors, and project partners following a natural disaster, gaining valuable experience in insurance claims, recovery efforts, and large-scale restoration projects.
 
At Rhoden Roofing, Ron works closely with commercial clients, school districts, municipalities, churches, and business owners to identify roofing and exterior solutions that align with their operational and financial goals. His background in capital planning, facility management, and financial stewardship allows him to serve as a trusted advisor throughout the decision-making process.
 
Ron and his wife are the proud parents of three children. When he’s not working with clients, you’ll likely find him at one of his children’s sporting events, on the golf course, cheering on the Wildcats or the Chiefs, or enjoying time with family and friends.
 

David Shultz
Lead Estimator

View Profile

Outside of work he spends most of his time with his wife and kids, supporting his kids’ activities, and working around the house doing home improvement projects. He enjoys vacationing to Colorado with family and would love to get back out on the ski slopes sometime.

Commercial Account Manager

As a proud dad of two kids, along with a house cat named Michael and a dog named Stanley, family is a core part of Zach’s life. In his free time, he enjoys playing country music around town and is an active runner. His diverse interests and warm personality help him connect with those around him.

Braden Taylor
Commercial Account Manager

View Profile

Braden shares his life with his lovely fiancé, Madi, and their two cats, Loki and Cheeto. A passionate car enthusiast, he enjoys being an active part of and contributing to the automotive community in Wichita.

Chuck Chandler
Commercial Superintendent

His experiences working on commercial roofs in both roles have honed his expertise in this area. Jose Hernandez
Commercial Service/Superintendent

View Profile

Sales Liaison

Rhonda Riggs
Office Coordinator

View Profile
Rhonda Riggs brings extensive experience in facilities maintenance coordination, customer service, and operational support to her role as Office Coordinator at Rhoden Roofing.  A graduate of Goddard High School and alumni of Friends University, she has built her career around delivering exceptional service and supporting efficient business operations.

Senior Claims Specialist

Kyle Mitchell
Claims Specialist

View Profile

Kyle is also a licensed appraiser in the state of Texas, bringing additional credibility and technical expertise to his work in property and casualty claims. Over the years, he has gained extensive field experience across numerous states, including Texas, Louisiana, Nevada, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Kansas, Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, and Ohio. His commitment to thorough evaluations and fair outcomes has made him a trusted resource to carriers, policyholders, and appraisal professionals alike.

Outside of work, Kyle enjoys spending quality time with friends and family. He’s also an avid outdoorsman with a passion for duck hunting and fishing whenever he can get outdoors.

Joseph Goodrum
Claims Specialist

View Profile
Joseph brings extensive experience in both commercial and residential construction, along with years of hands-on involvement in the property insurance claims process, to his role as a claims specialist. His background spans multiple trades including carpentry, refinishing and restoration work, insulation, and septic systems, providing a practical understanding of building systems and jobsite conditions that supports accurate scope development and well documented supplemental estimates.
 
Joseph is a United States Marine Corps veteran with prior experience working as a property adjuster on commercial and residential claims across numerous markets including Louisiana, Iowa, Ohio, Minnesota, Michigan, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Kansas. Known for clear communication and detail driven work, he applies real world construction knowledge and claims experience to help ensure projects are properly scoped and supported.
 
Outside of work, Joseph values being present for family life. He enjoys attending his children’s after-school activities, including sports and theater, and appreciates a slower pace whenever schedules allow.

Drew Murray
Head of Production

View Profile

Drew is attentive, thoughtful, and deeply knowledgeable about two things in particular: roofing and Rhoden Roofing. 

Born in Wichita, Drew began his Rhoden Roofing career in 2012 as a project coordinator. In that role, he refined his talent for listening carefully, identifying customer concerns, and simply paying attention to the details that determine a project’s success. That same attention to detail later made him a natural fit for commercial estimating, where patience and technical understanding are critical. 

Because his experience and knowledge could not be contained to one place, Drew eventually moved into the field full time as a production foreman. In 2021, he moved to Tampa, Florida, where he continued expanding his knowledge of building codes, installation methods, and roofing materials. 

Drew returned to his native Wichita and rejoined Rhoden Roofing in 2026 as Head of Production. In that role, he brings a calm, detail-oriented approach to each project and helps ensure that customers benefit from both his technical knowledge and his understanding of the Rhoden Roofing process. 

Outside of work, Drew enjoys golfing and spending time outdoors. Given his passion for roofing, one of those activities likely involves roofing. 

Haylee Standley
Production Planning Manager

View Profile

Haylee has a lot of experience coming from the customer service/service industry. She loves spending time outdoors, and camping at the lake with her husband, Cody, and their three children.  Aside from scheduling all of the jobs and ordering material at Rhoden Roofing, she enjoys spending her down time with her family and friends.

Meagan Kettler
Production Administrator

View Profile

Her background includes experience in commercial real state, finance, and higher education with Wichita State University, where her calm under pressure allowed her to optimize strategic operations.

Meagan joined Rhoden Roofing in 2026, bringing the strategic thinking needed to ensure production processes run smoothly. Raised in a large family and deeply rooted in the Wichita community, she excels at balancing competing priorities.

After meeting her husband in 2022, she has since found two new priorities in her two toddlers. On the weekends, she enjoys spending time outside, supported by a patio and a cold beer.

Zac Stetler
Residential Production Manager

View Profile

With a passion for business, he started Hudson Antique Market. Outside of work, Zac is a dedicated Kansas City Chiefs fan and enjoys playing golf as well as spending quality time with his family. He is married to his beautiful wife, Janelle, and they have two adorable daughters who bring joy to their lives.

James Ramos
Field Production Foreman

View Profile

James is a dedicated professional at Rhoden Roofing, where he began his journey in March 2024. With three years of experience in roof installation, James has developed a strong foundation in the roofing industry, complemented by his role as an assistant manager. His expertise also extends to remodeling both interior and exterior spaces, showcasing his versatility and commitment to quality craftsmanship.

Outside of work, James is passionate about fishing and cars, often spending his free time working on projects that fuel his enthusiasm for automotive culture. He enjoys sharing these interests with his family, which includes his wife and their five children. James’s love for family and hands-on work drives him to excel in both his personal and professional life.

Jose Ramirez
Field Production Foreman

View Profile

Lachlan Jones
Field Production Foreman

View Profile

Lachlan joined Rhoden Roofing in 2026 after a tenure teaching, bringing with him the same patience, communication skills, and steady demeanor required to be a positive influence on high schoolers — no small feat. 

Before joining Rhoden Roofing, Lachlan coached high school football in Rose Hill and worked as a personal trainer. He continues to stay active as a semi-active MMA fighter and kickboxer, experience that helps him maintain order among his French Bulldog, Corgi, and cat.

When he is not at work, Lachlan often plays video games. Between roofing, training, MMA, and kickboxing, it is one of the few times you will find him sitting down. 

 

Drake Zogleman
Field Production Foreman

View Profile

Drake takes pride in delivering top-quality workmanship and ensuring every project runs smoothly from start to finish. With a strong background in hands-on work, Drake brings attention to detail, leadership, and a commitment to excellence to every job site.

Outside of work, Drake enjoys spending time with friends and family, fishing, golfing, and camping. He’s passionate about the outdoors and values building great relationships with the people he works with and serves.

Jeff Davis
Field Production Foreman

View Profile

Jeff brings a well-rounded background in construction, public service, aircraft manufacturing, and management to his position as a field production foreman at Rhoden Roofing.

He worked as a 911 dispatcher and served as a police officer for 10 years. He later moved into aircraft manufacturing and management, building on the same level-headedness, attention to detail, and commitment to doing the right thing that now guide his work on roofing projects.
