Ryan O’Hare
Field Production Foreman

View Profile

Originally from the greater Chicago area, Ryan brings adaptability and a constant willingness to learn to Rhoden Roofing.

After serving in the Army, Ryan found his way to the Lower Midwest, where he and his wife are raising their children. His background also includes experience in aircraft work, which built an already well-developed understanding of systems and precision.

Whether he is at work or working around the house, Ryan likes to stay busy and approaches each project with curiosity and care. He is eager to understand how a roof system works, then disciplined enough to apply that knowledge where it matters.

Outside of work, Ryan enjoys fishing, camping, and cooking with his wife and kids. He also has two Great Danes – two more systems that require curiosity and particular care.

Jerrod Byrne
Quality Assurance & Warranty Manager

View Profile

Jerrod is a former fireman from Wichita, bringing a diverse background in general contracting, home inspections, and carpentry to his endeavors. With 14 years of experience in vocational ministry, he has dedicated much of his life to serving others. He has been happily married to his high school sweetheart for 25 years. Together, they are proud parents of two incredible adult children. In addition to his professional pursuits, Jarrod is a passionate musician and enjoys woodworking, but above all, he values time spent with family.

 

Noah Diver
Production Support

View Profile

Noah is a skilled professional with five years of experience in the aircraft industry and one year in construction. His diverse background equips him with a unique perspective on both technical and practical aspects of his work. Noah’s commitment to excellence and adaptability make him a valuable asset in any project he undertakes. As he continues to grow in his career, he is eager to apply his skills and knowledge to new challenges in the construction field.

Daniel Williams
Production Support

View Profile

Daniel grew up in Missouri and is a proud United States Air Force veteran, having served from 2005 to 2009. Previously, he worked in masonry and has a passion for sports, particularly cheering for the Kansas City Chiefs and Royals, as well as enjoying wrestling and fishing. Daniel loves spending time with his three children, cherishing moments spent together as a family.

Alex Fuentes
Production Support

View Profile

Alex Fuentes joined Rhoden Roofing in 2026, bringing a strong work ethic and a desire to keep learning.

A devoted father, Alex values hands-on experience and believes in applying what he learns in practical ways. He enjoys spending time outdoors, camping, exploring new places. As a firm believer in continual growth, he is always looking for opportunities to improve in everything he does.

At Rhoden Roofing, Alex brings that steady, willing-to-learn approach to a role that helps keep projects and crews moving and growing alongside him.
Seth Pearson
Head of Marketing
View Profile
Seth joined the team in 2022, with a diverse professional background including finance, consulting, public law enforcement, and restaurant promotion. His very first job was working and teaching for several years at a knitting shop! Seth is originally from Fort Collins, Colorado, but now lives in historic College Hill, Wichita with his wife Sidney. He attended University of Minnesota for degrees in Marketing and Entrepreneurial Management, and University of Denver for a Master’s in Business Administration.

Seth is our Marketing Lead and helps the team with internal and external communications, roofing education, and storytelling. You may also find him on a jobsite getting feedback about our process, constantly looking to improve the Rhoden Roofing customer experience.

McKenzey Bell
Video & Creative Manager

View Profile

McKenzey joined the team in 2023. Born and raised in Kansas, McKenzey pursued a degree in filmmaking with a minor in communications, studying at Hutchinson Community College and Wichita State University.

As the Video and Creative Manager, McKenzey oversees all aspects of video production and social media, ensuring that every project resonates with audiences.

In addition to filmmaking, McKenzey has a deep appreciation for movies, books, music, and games, often spending quality time with family and friends. A lover of short films, McKenzey enjoys collaborating with friends to create compelling narratives during their free time. A fun fact about McKenzey is that they are a percussionist, adding a rhythmic beat to both life and art.

Logan Gossett
Customer Relations/Content Manager

View Profile

Logan graduated from the University of Kansas in 2020 with a degree in Strategic Communication. His passion for connecting with people drives his work, whether through writing, presenting, engaging in conversation, or simply sharing a wave from afar. Communication provides him with the opportunity to listen to people’s stories, which is his favorite activity.

In 2023, Logan began working in the home exterior industry, joining Rhoden Roofing in 2024, where he’s accountable for many of the company’s communication efforts. His role blends strategic storytelling with customer engagement to enhance brand identity and build lasting relationships.

Outside of work, Logan enjoys spending time in his native town of Derby, KS with his wife, Kaley, and diving into the endless reading material queued in his browser tabs — always eager to learn something new.

Chloe Woolbright
Marketing/Communications Specialist

View Profile

Chloe is a Wichita native and Marketing & Communications Specialist with experience in digital marketing, content creation, copywriting, social media, branding, and campaign strategy. She earned her bachelor’s degree in English from Kansas State University and her master’s degree in Digital & Integrated Marketing Communications from the University of Kansas.

Outside of work, Chloe is a Chiefs fan and a one-person house divided between K-State and KU. In her free time, she enjoys crafting, creative projects, and spending time with family and friends.

Mike Rhoden
Head of Systems & AI

View Profile

Mike leads Systems and AI at Rhoden Roofing, a role that his curiosity makes him well suited for.

Before joining Rhoden Roofing, Mike served as Lead Software Engineer for a digital transformation firm. He earned his degree in math, philosophy, and computer science from Benedictine College, a combination that shows his ability to ask thoughtful questions, synthesize complex systems, and turn abstract ideas into something tangible. Mike is the adult version of the kid who never stopped asking “why?” Mike, however, never needs to ask twice.

At Rhoden Roofing, Mike improves the systems that support the customer experience. If a customer has ever wondered why Rhoden Roofing does something a certain way, odds are Mike has wondered about it, too – and likely improved it.

Mike lives with his wife and four children. A longtime soccer fan, he grew up cheering for the Wichita Wings and is a season-ticket holder for K-State Football. When he is not working or spending time with his family, he enjoys spending time outdoors and tending to his acreage.

Corey McKinney
IT Systems Administrator

View Profile
Born and raised in California, Corey has always had a passion for technology, service, and connection. After graduating high school, he proudly served four years in the United States Marine Corps, where he developed the discipline, leadership, and problem-solving mindset that continue to shape his professional life today.
With more than 20 years of experience in the IT industry, Corey has worked across industrial, government, educational, commercial, and enterprise environments — providing reliable, forward-thinking solutions to complex technical challenges. He holds multiple certifications in server support, networking, unified communications, and cybersecurity, reflecting his dedication to excellence and continuous learning.
 
Corey is a devoted husband to his wife, DaNell, and together they share a blended family of six children and nine grandchildren who keep life lively and full of joy. Outside of work, Corey is deeply involved in volunteering at his church, where he enjoys giving back to his community and serving others. When he’s not managing networks or mentoring others, you’ll likely find him flying, BBQing or smoking something flavorful, experimenting with 3D printing, collecting coins, or chillaxing with Netflix.
 
For Corey, technology isn’t just a career — it’s a lifelong pursuit of innovation, connection, and creativity, guided by family, faith, and a strong sense of purpose.

Jennifer Patterson
Head of Finance & Administration

View Profile

Jennifer brings over 20 years of experience with accounting, mergers and acquisitions, budgeting, and financial leadership to Rhoden Roofing.  She previously served as Director of Accounting for a facility management company, a role that required the same precision and cool headedness that she brings to Rhoden Roofing.

After graduating from Wichita State University, Jennifer earned her MBA from Friends University. She has remained in the Wichita area with her husband, two sons, and three miniature schnauzers. As the only girl in the house, she has had plenty of opportunity to practice patience, perspective, and leadership at home.

Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her family and traveling. From August through February, however, much of her free time is reserved for cheering on the Kansas City Chiefs.

Sarah Linder
Accounting Specialist

View Profile
Sarah is a Wichita native and a graduate of Wichita State University, where she earned her Bachelor’s degree in Business Management. Her professional background spans childcare and real estate, both of which strengthened her communication skills, attention to detail, and commitment to providing excellent service. She is motivated by creating smooth, stress-free experiences for the people she works with and enjoys contributing to an environment where others can succeed.

Sarah and her husband Chason were married in 2023. They can often be found traveling for a concert or enjoying the outdoors through camping and hiking. Sarah has a passion for creative hands-on projects, from home renovations to vegetable gardening and caring for her houseplants. She also cherishes quiet time at home with her husband and their cat, Suki.

Dana Koerner
Accounting Specialist

View Profile
Dana brings 25 years of accounting experience to Rhoden Roofing, along with a natural ability to make people feel comfortable. 
 
Most recently, Dana spent years working for USD 259 where her discipline, patience and ability to connect with anyone served her and the district well. A lifelong Wichita native, Dana brings warmth, perspective and a desire to leave both people and spreadsheets a little better than she found them. 
 
Outside of work, Dana enjoys music, sporting events, concerts and spending time by the water, whether that means a pool, lake, or the ocean. She also enjoys tossing a frisbee with her dog and working on her house. Three rooms into a remodel, Dana remains undaunted, which speaks volumes to her discipline. 

Lynnette Hilty
Recruiting & Onboarding Specialist

View Profile

Lynnette grew up in Canton, Kansas, and earned her Bachelor’s degree in Journalism from Iowa State University. She currently resides in Hutchinson, Kansas, where she has spent the last 17 years as a college recruiter, serving as the Assistant Director of Admissions.

Married to her husband Ryan, Lynnette is proud of their family, which includes a daughter and son, as well as a delightful  granddaughter. Together, Lynnette and Ryan share a passion for sports, frequently attending events and cheering for their favorite teams: the University of Oklahoma softball team, the Kansas Jayhawks and Iowa State basketball teams, and the Kansas City Chiefs football team.

When she’s not at work, you’ll likely find Lynnette at a HutchCC sporting event or enjoying the excitement of the College Softball World Series, an event she and Ryan love to attend as often as possible. Her enthusiasm for sports and community reflects her vibrant personality and dedication to nurturing the next generation.

Roof Inspections

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Get Your Free Roof Inspection that Identifies Problem Areas in Wichita

Even with the highest quality materials and the best roofers performing the installation, storms and age cause wear and tear on even the sturdiest of roofs. That’s why it’s necessary to have your roof checked periodically to ensure that it is functioning as it should.

Roof inspections are completed by qualified roofing team members who know exactly what to look for when it comes to damaged roofs. Hopefully, nothing will be found. However, there’s a chance you won’t even know that your roof has a problem until a trained professional has a look for themselves.

At Rhoden Roofing, our Wichita roofers perform quick and efficient roof inspections for our neighbors to ensure the safety of our community and long-lasting roofs. Whether there’s a leak causing water damage or you need to check to see if your home’s structure can handle heavier roofing, our trusted specialists are trained to identify even the tiniest of problems.

Call us today to schedule your free roof inspection to make sure everything is in tip top shape. We inspect various residential types of roofs from asphalt, metal, tile to cedar roofs.

We also provide real estate inspections that include a written report that you can send to both parties in a transaction for a fixed price of $200.

Get A FREE Estimate

Benefits of Regular Roof Inspections

It may seem tedious to hire a roofer to come to your home and inspect your roof, only to possibly find out that it’s in perfectly good condition and requires no repairs. It is easy to turn things like that into a chore; like going to the doctor’s office to check on the health of our bodies – you’ll always regret not getting a checkup if something ends up being wrong. That’s why we inspect our roofs.

The main benefit to routine roof inspections is that they save you hassle in the long term. From time and money to potentially dangerous outcomes, if a bad roof is left in disrepair for too long; it can end up costing you. Fixing a few leaks here and there instead of having to complete a full roof replacement is a much better tradeoff. It’s cheaper and can be done in just a day.

Plus, roof inspections ensure that there isn’t anything harmful lurking under the surface that you wouldn’t notice without the help of a professional. Even if you simply catch the early stages of a leak, an inspection could save you from dangerous consequences like mold that can seriously affect your health if left unattended.

Structural damage to your roofing like missing tiles or broken panels can also negatively affect the energy efficiency of your roof. Regular roof inspections ensure that you’re getting the most out of your investment by making sure your energy costs are as low as possible, and your roof is functioning the way it should.

Not to mention, you put much effort into choosing your perfect roof, and you probably saved up a lot of your hard earned money to pay for it. It is only natural to want it to continue looking good too. Roof inspections can help make sure your roof remains in prime shape with cleanings and proper care. Ready to have your roof adequately inspected? Give us a call!

Rhoden Roofing Performs Roof Inspections

Avoid a costly roof replacement and opt for regular roof inspections. Taking on smaller, quicker roof repairs will save you time and money in the long run and will ensure that your family is safe and sound beneath a sturdy shelter.

Contact Rhoden Roofing for a free roof inspection and be positive that you’re living under a stable and robust roof that will last for years to come. Call today!

Emergency Roof Repair

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Your Reliable Emergency Roof Repair Services in Wichita (Insurance Claims Available)

Sometimes damage to your home can happen at the most inconvenient times. Roof storm damage can be particularly brutal – it leaves your home exposed to external elements which could cause further damage to the home. This is why we can’t stress enough the importance of acting fast when your home is in need of emergency roof repair services.

Fortunately for you, Rhoden Roofing offers fast and efficient emergency roof repair services that can help you fix up the damage in no time.

Get A FREE Estimate

What Type of Roof Damage Requires Emergency Repair?

Roof damage can happen at any time, but it’s important to understand which events typically result in roof damage that requires emergency repair. Below, let’s take a look at the various types of roof damage Rhoden Roofing often sees when we’re called out to emergency jobs in Wichita.

Hail Damage

Storm damage caused by hail is less obvious than impact damage and the evidence can really only be seen on the roof. Hailstones can cause roofing granules to be compromised, or cause dents in materials like metal. You will need to get a professional roofer in to adequately assess the damage.

Wind Damage

The severe winds that come along with storm activity in Wichita can cause immeasurable damage. Your home’s roof may suffer missing or damaged shingles, and could be further affected by flying debris.

 

Water: A Home’s Worst Enemy

One of the many reasons that contacting an emergency roofing repair company is so important is to prevent water from entering your home. If water continues to enter your home, it may cause lasting damage that can result in significant expenses.

  • Water causes mold issues and may result in a variety of different harmful growths.
  • Water can warp and rot wood, which may cause significant structural problems that require extensive repair work.
  • Water damage may be destructive to the rest of your home in terms of damage to furniture, appliances and electronics.
Get A FREE Estimate

How Rhoden Roofing Can Help

At Rhoden Roofing, we provide emergency roof repair services that help you prevent further issues occurring within your home. Once you contact one of our team members, we’ll send someone to your home immediately to assess the damage. Next, we’ll develop a plan of attack that will help prevent further damage and begin the process of repairing your roof.

Quickly Seal Off Your Roof

In many cases, we’ll start by sealing your roof off to ensure that water and other debris won’t enter your home. Then, we’ll begin to perform the roof restoration process that will return your current roof to its normal state.

Assist with Filing an Insurance Claim

Rhoden Roofing is here to help you sort out your roof damage insurance claims. If you have a damage insurance policy on your home, it’s likely that your insurance provider is responsible for paying some or all of the costs.

Approaching a claim incorrectly can result in a lack of compensation. Our team can provide you with the advice and documentation you need to ensure the smooth processing of your insurance claim.

Get in Touch Today

We are an emergency roof repair specialist with years of experience providing customers with excellent services in Wichita, KS. We understand what it takes to prevent further damage to your home, and we’re always here to offer advice and suggestions on how to best approach emergency roof damage.
It’s essential to get in touch with our team of roofing experts as quickly as possible. Call us in your time of need for a free inspection.

Your Trusted Organic Mat-Based Shingles Contractor in Wichita, KS

The various types of asphalt shingles all have similar compositions, but are differentiated by the materials used within those compositions. In the case of organic mat-based shingles, they include a base layer of cellulose made up of wood chips, and recycled cardboard, rags and paper. This cellulose met, or felt, is thicker than fiberglass, making it more durable.

Rhoden Roofing is the organic shingles expert in Wichita, having installed and repaired a great many roofs in the area over the years. Feel free to speak to us regarding your organic shingles roofing needs. We’re on stand-by to provide unbiased roofing advice and a free inspection.

Types of Organic Mat-Based Shingle Roofs

Any type of asphalt shingle variety commonly comes in two types, which differ greatly in cost, durability and the overall finish.

Three-Tab Organic Mat-Based Shingles

Three-tab shingles are the more affordable option, though it does not offer much variety in terms of its look. They only come in one size and shape, which delivers a generally flat-looking roof surface. One of the big advantages of three-tab shingles is its light weight, which is sometimes an important consideration given what the home’s structure can bear.

Architectural Organic Mat-Based Shingles

These are also known as 3D or laminate shingles. One of the major draw cards of architectural shingles is its variety of shapes and sizes, as opposed to the uniform look of three-tab shingles. It is such that homeowners will be able to mimic the look of more premium roofing alternatives, like slate and cedar. Individual architectural shingles are also thicker, making them more durable and longer-lasting.

Advantages of Organic Mat-Based Shingles

Durability

Organic mat-based shingles’ base layer of cellulose together with the double layer of asphalt means it offers superior strength and durability.

Versatility

Though only offered by architectural organic shingles, homeowners love the fact that they can determine exactly what their organic shingle roof can look like. There are no restrictions of uniformity, enabling every homeowner to achieve a unique look.

Easy Installation

Installing organic shingles is a simple process that could even be DIY’d by homeowners that are adventurous enough. This ease of installation also impacts overall costs as labor requirements are less than it would be for a typical residential roofing alternative.

WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE

Reactive vs. Proactive Roof Maintenance

Reactive Maintenance

Fix it when it leaks.

  • Leaks, stains, or tenant trigger a call to a roofer.
  • Minor damage has more time to saturate insulation or cause interior damage.
  • Emergency repairs are up to 7x more likely and harder to budget around.
  • Can cost 3-9x more than planned maintenance over the course of the roof’s life.
  • Roof life is shortened when water intrusion goes unnoticed.

Lower commitment, higher risk. 

Proactive Maintenance

Inspect and maintain to prevent problems from escalating.

  • Scheduled inspections help identify issues before they cause interior damage.
  • Vulnerable areas, such as pitch pockets, pipes, and membrane tears are re-sealed as needed.
  • Maintenance reduces emergency repairs and stabilizes annual budgeting.
  • A maintained membrane roof has an extended roof life compared with an unmaintained roof.
  • Documentation sustains the roof’s warranty.

How much does RoofCare cost?

RoofCare starts at $998 annually for roofs up to 200 squares (20,000 square feet). If your roof is larger than 200 squares, give us a call so we can discuss options that will work for you. 

Which commercial roofs qualify for RoofCare?

RoofCare is designed for commercial roofs that can be maintained in their current condition. If a roof has active leaks, saturated substrate or damage that prevents proper maintenance, repairs may be recommended before the roof is enrolled. 

Is RoofCare included with a commercial roof replacement?

Yes. Complete roof replacements include two years of RoofCare at no cost. After the second year, RoofCare continues at the standard annual rate unless the owner decides to cancel.

What is included in a RoofCare inspection?

A RoofCare inspection includes a condition review with photo documentation, routine maintenance items and minor repairs, and recommendations for larger repairs, monitoring, or future budgeting. 

Does RoofCare include emergency roof repairs?

RoofCare includes priority emergency service within 24-48 hours of notification, depending on access and demand. 

How does RoofCare provide bond planning support?

Our team has a dedicated K-12 specialist with years of experience gaining bond funds and presenting to board members. We apply that experience to provide school districts with the data and reporting they need to ensure their portfolio is protected.

Commercial Metal Roofing

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Commercial Metal Roof Repair and Replacement Specialist in Wichita

Metal roofs have many distinct advantages over other roofing materials, which make them a popular choice for commercial roofing in Wichita. ​ They are durable, lightweight, easy to install and are fireproof. With a wide variety of colors and styles to choose from, Rhoden Roofing can achieve virtually any look you want for your commercial property from office buildings, hotels, warehouses to multi-family roofing projects.

Get A FREE Estimate

Types of Metal Roofing

Metal offers a wide spectrum of variations and materials under its umbrella, all of which can be installed by Rhoden Roofing. These are some of the most popular metal roofing varieties installed on commercial facilities:

Aluminium Roofing

Aluminium roofing has many benefits that business owners and property managers are attracted to. While it is durable, corrosion-resistant, cost-effective, and eco-friendly, aluminum roofing also doesn’t rust, enables smoother water runoff, and reflects the sun better than other metal roofing materials. This also makes it energy-efficient.

Steel Roofing

A popular choice for roofing in hail-prone areas particularly, steel roofing is super durable and low maintenance, which ranks it high on the longevity scale. Like most metal roofing materials, the heat reflection also contributes to reduced energy use and costs.

Standing Seam Metal Roofing

Standing-seam is the most popular iteration of metal roofing. Essentially, this type of roofing raises the seams beyond the level of the actual roof, thereby creating panels that run from the ridge to the eaves of the roof. Its interlocking system ensures that a watertight seal is created, and also makes it one of the strongest, most reliable roof systems on the market today.

Corrugated Metal Roofing

Corrugated metal is made from galvanized steel rolled into a wavy pattern. This corrugation process enhances the strength of the material, making corrugated metal a tough metal roofing option ideal for commercial properties. This is thanks to its light weight, durability and water-shedding features.

Advantages to Metal Roofs

Metal is one of the most reliable roofing materials on the market for commercial and industrial buildings. These are some of the characteristics that make it a great roofing option:

Durability

Metal roofing holds up well against all types of harsh weather conditions. It is even able to withstand debris and animal activity. The impact of extreme weather in the Wichita area makes metal roofing an excellent choice for durability.

Low maintenance

Maintenance on a metal roof is so easy that you could almost install it and forget about it. As with any roofing material, regular maintenance is a must, but the upkeep on a metal roof is so limited, that compared to other solutions, you’ll have a worry-free roof and save on costs in the long run.

Longevity

Its durability and ease of maintenance contribute to metal roofs lasting a very long time – up to 50-70 years. This is great news for any business as costs are significantly saved in the long run, considering regular commercial roof maintenance is observed.

Environmentally friendly

In most cases, a quality metal roof will be made of anything from 35% – 95% recyclable and/or recycled material. While the lifespan of a metal roof will be very long, when it does come time to remove it for whatever reason, the entire thing will be 100% recyclable, as opposed to being dumped in a landfill. In addition, its heat-reflecting capabilities means the homeowner will save on home energy costs too, by reducing the need for cooling in the home.

Value

While a commercial metal roof will cost more up front to install, it will cost less over its lifetime. The long-term investment is well worth it considering the reduction of maintenance and repair costs over the roof’s lifetime. On top of that, metal roof warranties also tend to be exceptional.

Full-Service Residential Roofing for Wichita Homeowners

Rhoden Roofing provides home roofing services Kansas homeowners can rely on for roof installation, replacement, repair, storm damage support, or a professional inspection. We help Wichita homeowners choose the right roofing solution for their home, budget, and long-term protection.

Residential Roof Installation

New roofing installation is a major project for any homeowner. As local new roof installers in Wichita, Rhoden Roofing makes it our mission to help the process run smoothly and efficiently while advising homeowners every step of the way.

A proper roof installation includes more than putting on new shingles. Our team looks at decking, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, roof edges, material selection, and manufacturer requirements. Whether you’re building a new home, adding onto your property, or replacing an outdated system with better materials, we’ll help you choose a roof that fits your home and Wichita weather.

Residential Roof Replacement

Rhoden Roofing will always advocate for repairs before replacement when repairs make sense. In some cases, a roof replacement is simply the better long-term decision. That may be true if your roof has recurring leaks, widespread storm damage, missing shingles, granule loss, poor ventilation, or materials near the end of their service life.

When replacement is needed, we focus on the highest level of workmanship from inspection through final cleanup. Our team explains the condition of your roof, helps you compare materials, and walks you through warranty options so you can make a confident decision.

Residential Roof Repair

Major and minor roof repairs can make the difference between a roof that still has useful life and one that continues to decline. Missing shingles, flashing problems, small leaks, storm damage, and ventilation issues should be inspected before water reaches decking, insulation, drywall, or interior finishes.

The roof repair experts at Rhoden Roofing are trained and experienced in the details of roofing. We inspect the surrounding roof system, so homeowners know whether the problem is isolated or part of a larger issue.

Roofing Materials Built for Wichita Homes and Weather

Rhoden Roofing installs a variety of residential roof types. The right material should match your home’s appearance, your budget, and the weather conditions common in Wichita.

Asphalt Shingle Roofs

Asphalt shingle roofs are one of our most popular home roofing options. Due to their affordability, durability, and style flexibility, they’re a top choice for many Wichita homes.

Using high-quality materials and careful installation practices, our residential roofing experts install asphalt roofing systems designed to be sturdy, reliable, and long-lasting.

Metal Roofs

More homeowners are choosing metal roofing because it can offer strong value over time. Metal roofs last longer, are weather-resistant, and are easy to maintain when installed correctly.

While the upfront investment may be higher than some roofing options, metal can be a strong choice for homeowners who want durability, wind performance, and lower maintenance needs over the life of the roof.

Flat and Low-Slope Roofs

Although not as common in residential areas as other roof types, flat and low-slope roofs are an option for some homes, additions, porches, garages, and specialty roof areas.

These roofs require the right material and careful installation because drainage, seams, and flashing details matter. If you’re considering a flat roof or need service on a low-slope residential roof area, Rhoden Roofing can help you understand the best option.

Cedar Roofs

Cedar roofs add a distinct, natural finish to the home. They can be a worthy long-term investment for homeowners who want character, curb appeal, and a roofing material with a strong visual impact.

Cedar also requires proper installation and maintenance. Rhoden Roofing helps homeowners determine whether cedar makes sense for their home’s design, budget, and Kansas weather conditions.

Tile Roofs

Tile roofs are made from clay or concrete and are known for durability, low maintenance, and resistance to rot and mildew. In the right application, tile can last for decades and provide a premium look.

Tile is not the right fit for every home. Roof structure, weight, design, and installation experience all matter. Rhoden Roofing helps homeowners evaluate whether tile roofing is practical for their property.

Slate Roofs

Slate is one of the most durable and distinctive residential roofing materials available. Its natural appearance gives a home a premium finish, and its long lifespan is made possible by the material’s strength.

Because slate is a specialty roofing system, proper installation is critical. Rhoden Roofing has experience with premium materials and can help homeowners decide whether slate is a good fit for their home, structure, and budget.

Roofing Challenges and Warning Signs for Wichita Homes

Wichita homes face a mix of roofing concerns. Older homes may have aging shingles, worn flashing, outdated ventilation, or hidden decking issues. Newer homes can still develop problems after hail, high winds, heavy rain, or repeated heat exposure. Across the city, Kansas weather can test any roofing system.

Your roof may need a closer look if you notice:

  • Shingles that are missing, curled, cracked, or lifting along the edges.
  • Ceiling stains that show up after rain, even if they dry out later.
  • Loose or damaged flashing around chimneys, vents, skylights, or roof transitions.
  • Shingle granules collecting near downspouts, gutters, or the base of the home.
  • Dents on gutters, vents, flashing, or other metal roof components after hail.
  • Uneven roof areas, soft spots, or sections that appear to sag.
  • Leaks that appear during wind-driven rain or after a strong storm.
  • Gutters pulling away, overflowing, or allowing water to sit near roof edges.
  • A roof that looks worn, patchy, or close to the end of its expected lifespan.

As a local roofing contractor in Sedgwick County, Rhoden Roofing understands how Wichita weather affects both older roof systems and newer homes. A professional inspection helps determine whether repair, replacement, or continued monitoring makes the most sense before small roofing problems become more expensive.

Wichita Residential Roofing Questions Answered

Wichita homeowners often have questions about roof age, storm damage, repairs, replacement, and what to expect during the roofing process. These answers can help you understand when to schedule an inspection and what options may be available.

How do I know if my roof needs to be replaced?

Your roof may need to be replaced if it has recurring leaks, widespread storm damage, missing shingles, heavy granule loss, poor ventilation, or materials near the end of their expected lifespan. A roof inspection can help determine whether replacement is necessary or if repair is still practical.

Can you replace part of a roof?

Yes, part of a roof can sometimes be replaced if the damage is isolated and matching materials are available. In the case of shingles or tiles, replacing the faulty parts may restore the roof to good order. If the damage spans a large area, replacing the roof may be the more cost-effective option over time.

How often should you change your roof?

How often you should change your roof depends on the roofing material, installation quality, ventilation, storm exposure, and maintenance history. Many asphalt shingle roofs last 20 to 30 years, but Kansas hail, wind, and heat can shorten that lifespan.

Do I need a roof inspection after a hailstorm?

Yes, you should schedule a roof inspection after a hailstorm if your Wichita home was in the storm path. Hail can bruise shingles, damage vents, dent gutters, and loosen roofing components before interior water damage appears.

Does Rhoden Roofing help with insurance claims?

Yes. Rhoden Roofing helps homeowners with documentation for storm damage and support for roof insurance claims. We can inspect the roof, provide photos, explain the roofing scope, and assist during the claims process when appropriate.

What residential roofing materials does Rhoden Roofing install?

Rhoden Roofing installs asphalt shingles, metal roofing, flat and low-slope roofing, cedar roofing, tile roofing, and slate roofing. The right option depends on your home’s structure, budget, style, and long-term goals.

Does Rhoden Roofing offer documented inspections for real estate transactions?

Yes. Rhoden Roofing has a dedicated account manager who provides documented inspections for real estate transactions. Homeowners, buyers, sellers, and real estate professionals can learn more through our Real Estate Preferred Partner Program.

The Premier Seamless Gutter Installation in Wichita

When investing in a seamless gutter system in Wichita, you’re buying a guarantee. That after the gutter installation, you’ll never have to worry about leaks, again. Seamless means there’s no seams that could leak. It’s impossible.

At Rhoden Roofing, we install seamless gutter systems designed to last. Our gutter systems ensure leaks don’t send water around the foundation of your house, into the basement, or cause any other types of issues.

How We’re Different

Our Wichita gutter systems are designed with integrity and strength in mind. Whether the system expands, contracts, or freezes due to inclement weather, there will be no impact to your seamless gutters. Our seamless steel systems our designed to function perfectly in every type of weather.

Not only that, our seamless gutter installations look great. Seamless gutters add a sense of style to a home that traditional gutters simply cannot compete with. We offer custom cut gutters on-site. These gutters offer an exact fit and perfectly blend into the styling of your home.

With a plethora of different seamless gutter colors and styles available, we’ve found seamless gutter systems can actually increase the curb appeal of your house. Don’t let your gutter system look like an afterthought. Work with the professionals at Rhoden Roofing and get top quality seamless gutters installed perfectly.

Get A FREE Estimate

The Benefits of Seamless Gutters

One thing many customers love about seamless gutters is how strong they are. It doesn’t matter how bad the weather gets, a properly installed seamless gutter system will stay the course and avoid leakage, especially when compared with sectional gutters. This is because seamless gutters do not have miters that join the different pieces together.

Seamless means the gutter system has no seams. Without seams, there’s no potential for leaks. The more seams a system has the more likely the gutters will leak. Plus, sectional gutters tend to be made of weaker materials, which makes them more susceptible to leaking and damages.

If your seamless gutter system does need repairing down the road, this can be more difficult. Seamless gutter systems often need to be completely replaced if they need repaired. When compared with sectional gutters, this can be costly. However, a properly installed seamless gutter should not require repairs for more than a decade. 

Costs

From a cost perspective, seamless gutters tend to cost about the same as sectional gutters once you factor in overall costs. Sectional gutters require extra pieces, more maintenance, caulking, and a variety of tools. Plus, sectional gutters often do not last as long as seamless gutters. 

If you’re looking for a long lasting gutter solution, seamless gutters in Wichita are ideal. At Rhoden Roofing, we’re fans of seamless solutions and these gutter systems will ensure you avoid leaks for years to come. 

Stop settling for sectional gutters! Give us a call today and learn more about seamless gutters for your home.

Urethane Roof Coatings

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Urethane Roof Coating Application

Urethane roof coatings are some of the strongest roofing materials on the market. They’re ideal for high traffic areas because they’re flexible, seamless, and durable. They expand and contract with your roof’s surface, so they don’t endure as much stress as the seasons change.

Urethane resists water pooling, is more impact-resistant, is easy to apply, and is affordable. It’s a great way to protect your roof and give it extra years of life without paying for a brand-new roof. Learn more about our roof coating services here.

Get A FREE Estimate

Why Install a Urethane Roof Coating?

A urethane roof coating provides you with flexibility and durability. It can withstand the seasonal changes of your roof without losing its strength, giving it a long life. It can also withstand heavy impacts and works well for roofs with high traffic. It’s water-resistant, so you won’t see the same ponding you see with other types of coatings, making it less slippery when it’s wet.

Urethane roof coatings will adhere to almost any commercial roofing surface, so it’s ideal for nearly every building and any purpose. You can apply them to EPDM, TPO, BUR, metal, modified bitumen, spray polyurethane foam, and single-ply roofs.

A urethane roof coating provides your building with the UV protection it needs. It’s highly reflective, and it will deflect the sun in the summer to keep your building cooler, lowering your air conditioning costs. This not only reduces your building temperature but can extend the life of the roof by protecting it from the sun’s harmful rays.

Types of Urethane Roof Coatings

There are two primary types of urethane roof coatings: aromatic and aliphatic. Aromatic urethane coatings are not UV stable, but they are less expensive than aliphatic coatings. Aromatic coatings are best used as a base coat before applying another layer.

Aliphatic urethane coatings are more expensive, but they hold color, stay clean, and are UV stable. They work great on top of an aromatic coating, so your roof stays cleaner and deflects the sun’s rays. Even more, it won’t collect water and will be resistant to daily traffic.

How to Apply a Urethane Roof Coating

Urethane roof coatings can be a challenge to apply, and they produce a strong odor. It’s best to leave the application process to a professional with the appropriate equipment. A urethane roof coating company can advise you on the best practices while they install your roof, which typically includes recirculating air from inside the building or turning your HVAC off completely while installation takes place.

It’s always important to clean your roof before a urethane roof coating is applied. A urethane roof coating contractor will ensure that all issues are fixed and holes are patched before the coating is installed. While urethane roof coatings are typically sprayed, if the equipment isn’t properly cleaned or maintained, there may be issues.

It’s also important to ensure that the installation goes quickly because once urethane roof coating materials are opened, they don’t last long. The solvent cures quickly, even in the container, so be sure to enlist the help of a professional. That’s where Rhoden Roofing can help.

Get A FREE Estimate

Urethane Roof Coating Cost

As with any other roof coating material, urethane roof coating costs much less than a new roof. However, for an accurate estimate on your project, it’s best to give us a call. We can assess your roof and determine the exact cost for you.

Investing in a urethane roof coating will cost you a bit right now but not nearly as much as replacing your roof. It also saves you money in other areas of building maintenance. The bright white color reflects the sun and keeps your building cooler. This helps reduce your air conditioning bills.

The life these coatings add to your roof also prevents you from having to replace your roof as often, saving you even more money and providing you with a great value. When sprayed on, the liquid fills in seams, cracks, and vulnerable areas.

When the installation is done correctly, the operations in your facility won’t be interrupted for long, if at all, ensuring that you experience minimal downtime and revenue loss.

When it comes to restoring, protecting, and adding life to your commercial roof, urethane is one of the best coatings money can buy. Steel roofing provides many of the same great benefits as all other metal roofing systems. It’s durable, eco-friendly, and cost-effective. However, it also has a zinc coating that increases its resilience and provides it with an extra layer of corrosion resistance.

This type of metal roofing is a popular choice among homeowners and businesses in the Wichita area, where Rhoden Roofing are the trusted steel roofing experts. Speak to us today to learn more about steel roofing or allow us to provide a free, no-obligation quote.

Types of Steel Roof Coatings

The two types of steel roofs are determined by their coatings.

Galvanized Steel

Galvanized steel is coated with a thin layer of zinc to make it more corrosion resistant. It can be coated in various thicknesses depending on the homeowner’s preference and how it will be used.

Galvalume Steel

Galvalume is a trademarked product that contains an aluminum-zinc alloy mixture and is slightly more protective than galvanized steel. It holds up better over time and is a popular extra measure against rust and corrosion.

Advantages of a Steel Roof

Fire Resistant

Steel roofing is more fire-resistant than other metal roofing types. It can prevent a fire from spreading and insulates the home from sparking. It has a Class A noncombustible rating, which is the highest rating possible, so you can rest assured your home is at its safest with a steel roof.

Recyclable

Steel roofing is 100% recyclable. It won’t end up in a landfill, and it’s so lightweight that transportation and installation are much cheaper than other roofing types.

Cost Effective

Steel roofing is extremely cost-effective. It can save you money on your HVAC bills in both the summer and the winter by deflecting the sun and insulating heat. It regulates the temperature inside your home efficiently, so your systems don’t have to work as hard. Another cost-saver is the fact steel roofing can be installed over an existing roof, foregoing the cost of removal and hauling away.

Cleans Easily

Steel resists the build-up of algae and other bacteria. A good rain storm can clean your steel roof for you, and in the winter, snow will slide off instead of adding extra weight and pressure to the frame of your home.

Longevity

The average lifespan of a steel roof is 50 years or more, so you’ll enjoy the long lasting effects of all these other benefits for as long as you own your home. What’s more, it will increase your curb appeal and resale value.

Standing Seam Metal Roofs

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Standing Seam Metal Roofing Professionals Serving Wichita, KS

Standing seam metal roofing is made from interlocking panels, which make the seams stand up higher than the roof itself. This interlocking system makes it the strongest, most reliable roofing system on the market today. It is completely waterproof and comes in a variety of colors so you can customize it however you want.

Rhoden Roofing has installed and repaired countless standing seam metal roofs in the Wichita area and surrounds, so our team of expert roofers are on the pulse of new developments and products and techniques. Give us a call today for a free consultation!

Get A FREE Estimate

Types of Standing Seam Metal Roofing

Standing seam metal roofing comes in a variety of configurations. Each one interlocks a little bit differently, and they all provide different types of protection.

Snap-Lock

Snap-lock roofing systems have special edges that snap together with a male leg and a female leg. It doesn’t require the standing seam metal roof contractor to hand or mechanically fasten because they are secured by a simple click in place. Since this requires less labor, it results in lower costs. Snap-lock roofing can be installed in any environment as long as it is installed according to manufacturer specifications.

Mechanical Lock

Mechanical lock roofing systems have edges that line up together. Once lined up, they require the use of a mechanical seamer to bend and secure them in place. They come in single lock and double lock profiles for better performance and insulation in colder weather.

Batten Panel

Batten panel roofing systems have edges that line up together and are secured by a metal cap to create the seam. Depending on the type of cap, some are more secure than others. The more secure the cap, the better the roofing system will perform in inclement weather environments.

Advantages of Standing Seam Metal Roofing

Durable

Remember, standing seam metal roofing systems are still metal roofing systems, which means it is amongst the most durable roofing types on the market. Standing seam metal roofs have the extra benefit of concealed fasteners, which are not exposed to the elements that could deteriorate them over time. Its installation is also done in such a way that allows freedom of movement and therefore less breakage.

Customizable

Standing seam metal roofs are highly customizable, allowing homeowners to choose from a wide range of colors, lengths, widths, thicknesses, and seam types. Importantly, these customizations will not interfere with the stability of the seams, unlike other metal roofing alternatives.

Energy efficient

Just like other metal roofing, standing seam helps regulate the temperature in the home because it reflects the sun, saving you energy and money on heating and cooling bills.

Long-lasting

Standing seam metal roofs are in it for the long run! They can last up to one hundred years with regular, professional roofing maintenance and repairs.

Your Top Local Slate Roofing Specialist in Wichita


Slate roofing is the top of the line when it comes to all natural, extremely durable, and energy efficient roofing. Lasting for over a century, slate tiles instantly add market value to a property, are fireproof, waterproof, and are a stunning feature for any home.

Wichita’s Rhoden Roofing has experts in slate roofing to help you with your next renovation. From installation to slate roof repair and everything in between, we’re your local Wichita roofers who get the job done right. Professional craftsmanship is necessary for these impressive roofs to live up to their reputation and our roofing specialists are beyond capable of working with them.

Are you interested in a brand new slate roof that will turn heads throughout the neighborhood? Call us today and set up your free consultation with a trusted roofing contractor from Rhoden Roofing.

Benefits of Slate Roofing

Slate tiles are made of stone or rock and have a lot of significant benefits when used as a roofing material. They’re beautiful in appearance, durable, and last for long periods of time. Here’s some of the most common reasons people choose to install slate roofing tiles:

  • Longevity – One of the most significant benefits of slate roofing is that they last anywhere from 60 to 150 years. In short, you won’t need to replace slate roofing which makes it rather cost effective if the initial installation pricing is within your budget.
  • Appearance – It also looks wonderful and is an all natural material. The dark stone look is a feature of many homes, and since not many people have slate roofing, your home will stand out and look unique. Even further, slate roof tiles offer choices like varying size and thickness, as well as a wide array of color options
  • Energy Efficient & Environmentally Friendly – Another massive benefit of hiring slate roofers is that they will make your home super energy efficient. Slate tiles are naturally dark in color and absorb heat when it’s hot outside and releases it when the weather cools off, which will save you tons of money on your energy bills and help to offset the initial cost. Roofing waste, mainly asphalt shingles, accounts for more than 5% of waste in landfills every year. Slate is an easy choice to help with that reduction.
  • Fire Resistant – Slate roofing is one of the most fireproof roofs available. Unlike many other roofing materials like asphalt and cedar, slate tiles themselves are completely fire proof.

The Cons of Slate Roofs

The main concern people have when considering a slate roof is the price. Slate roof cost is one of the highest on the market, and it’s not to be taken lightly. On top of the cost of materials, hiring skilled tradespeople to install it properly will cost you even more. Here’s some things to take note of:

  • Find a Contractor That Knows Slate – Many roofing contractors have limited knowledge on slate roofs. Unfortunately, many try to install them anyways due to the high profit margins. When hiring a contractor, be sure to get references and ask about their experience.
  • Weight – Slate roofing tiles can wiegh over 1,000 pounds per square meaning you’ll need to make sure your home or business structure is sound before installing them.
  • Fragile – Slate is extremely fragile and can cause issues for anyone attempting to walk around on the roof. One misstep can cause thousands of dollars of damage in broken tiles.

Slate Roofing Costs in Wichita

Weighing the cost vs return on investment is the biggest concern for most homeowners installing slate roofs.  Slate roofing tile cost can range anywhere from $2,000 to $4,000 per square, and sometimes up to $8,000 with installation costs. That’s around 4 to 5 times more than the typical roofing material.  Obviously, the cost can be justified however since roofs can last up to 5 times longer.

Rubber Roof Coating

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Rubber Roof Coating Services

Many commercial buildings have rubber roofs for protection. Rubber roofs provide exceptional durability and protection, but they need to be maintained to keep them in tip-top shape. If your rubber roof has seen better days, but you don’t want to shell out the big bucks to fix it, a rubber roof coating may be what you’re after.

Different roofs take different types of coatings. There’s no one size fits all solution, but our rubber roof coating company can help determine what’s best for you. There are many different types of coatings on the market, and they all serve different purposes.

Get A FREE Estimate

Why Should You Apply a Coating?

Applying a coating to your rubber roof, as with any other roof coating, is easier and more affordable than installing a new roof. Rubber coatings are a slightly more expensive option, but they’re incredibly durable.

A rubber roof coating can prevent moisture seepage and leaks as well as more effectively insulate your building. With increased temperature regulation, you’ll save money on your heating and cooling bills. It protects your building from harmful UV rays and becomes an insulator of heat in the winter.

Rubber roof coatings prevent debris from sticking to your roof, so while it may accumulate, it will be much easier to clean. It protects your roof from corrosion, prevents water leaks, and makes your building more energy efficient.

You can postpone replacing your roof for at least 10 years, and often up to 30 years, with a rubber roof coating because it extends the life of your current roof. Best of all, the rubber roof coating needs very little maintenance. Rubber roof coatings also have elastic properties that allow it to expand and contract with your roof, and it won’t incur stress from the change of seasons.

Types of Rubber Roof Coatings

There are two types of rubber roof coating: rubber sheet coating and liquid rubber coating. Most rubber roof coating will fall into one of these two categories. If you need a coating outside of these two types, a professional rubber roof coating service would be able to help you determine what best suits your building.

RUBBER SHEET COATING

Rubber sheet coating is sold in sheets and requires an adhesive for installation. The adhesive can be expensive, and it’s best to have professional rubber roof coating contractors carry out the work. It requires some training and expertise in applying the adhesive and laying the sheets.

The tricky installation process makes rubber sheet coating slightly more expensive to install, but there are a variety of shapes, styles, and patterns, so you can choose what you like from a variety of options or customize your own.

Rubber sheet coating is perfect for commercial installations because when you order the material in bulk, you have more options. The interlocking sheets provide better protection over large areas and can provide moisture seepage prevention.

LIQUID RUBBER COATING

Liquid rubber coatings are very easy to apply and are less expensive than other rubber coatings. They brush on like paint and will immediately bind to your existing roof. Your budget can determine how many coats you use, but you can apply as many layers of liquid rubber as you like to suit your needs.

Liquid rubber coatings come in many colors, so you get to choose which you like the best. A rubber roof coating company can help you decide which color would best suit your needs as far as sun reflection and insulation if those are your main concerns.

Applying and Maintaining Rubber Roof Coatings

The process for applying a rubber roof coating varies depending on the type of coating and how it’s sold. Some are applied with adhesive and others are brushed on like paint. The adhesive variety is more complex and requires the expertise of a professional.

After you have your rubber roof coating installed, maintaining it is easy. It requires very little upkeep or attention. It’s extremely durable and resilient and will add decades of life to your existing roof.

Get A FREE Estimate

Rubber Roof Coating Cost

Rubber roof coating costs can vary depending on the type you use and the size of your building. Rubber roof coatings can be more costly than other types of coatings, but they’re incredibly durable and add more life to your roof than any other coating type.

If you have a rubber roof or are pursuing rubber roof coatings for your building, contact Rhoden Roofing. We can help you assess your needs, customize your solution, and provide you with a free quote. If you’re looking for durability and flexibility, check out Urethane roof coating. How Do You Know When It Is Time to Replace Your Roof?

A roof does not need to be actively leaking to need replacement. Hail, wind, UV exposure, heat, freezing temperatures, and normal aging can all wear down a Wichita roofing system over time.

Common signs that replacement may be needed include:

  • Recurring leaks or ceiling stains
  • Missing, lifted, cracked, or brittle shingles
  • Heavy granule loss
  • Hail damage across multiple roof slopes
  • Soft or damaged decking
  • Repeated repairs that no longer solve the problem
  • A roof nearing the end of its expected service life
  • Shingles that are discontinued or difficult to match

One damaged area does not automatically mean the entire roof needs to be replaced. An inspection can determine whether the issue is isolated or part of a larger system failure.

Roof Repair vs. Roof Replacement: Which Makes More Sense?

Roof repair is usually appropriate when damage is limited and the surrounding roofing materials are still in good condition.

Roof replacement becomes more practical when problems are widespread, leaks keep returning, materials are badly worn, or repairs are becoming frequent and expensive.

The decision usually comes down to three questions:

  1. Can the damaged area be repaired correctly?
  2. How much useful life remains in the rest of the roof?
  3. Will another repair provide better value than replacement?

Rhoden Roofing handles both repairs and replacements. If a repair will solve the problem responsibly, we will explain that. If the roof has reached the point where replacement makes more sense, we will show you why.

What Affects Roof Replacement Cost in Wichita?

Roof replacement cost depends on more than square footage. Roof design, materials, existing damage, and installation requirements can all change the final price.

The biggest cost factors include:

  • Roof size: Larger roofs require more materials and labor.
  • Pitch and complexity: Steep slopes, valleys, dormers, chimneys, and transitions increase installation time.
  • Material choice: Asphalt shingles, metal, slate, tile, cedar, and composite systems have different price points.
  • Tear-off: Multiple roofing layers can increase labor and disposal costs.
  • Decking condition: Damaged or rotted decking must be corrected before installation.
  • Ventilation and flashing: Proper airflow, underlayment, flashing, and roof accessories are part of a complete system.
  • Warranty options: Enhanced manufacturer warranties may require qualifying products and installation systems.

The lowest bid is not always the lowest long-term cost. Installation quality, material performance, and warranty protection all affect the value of the finished roof.

Are Class 4 Impact-Resistant Shingles Worth It?

For many Wichita homeowners, Class 4 impact-resistant shingles are worth considering because hail is a frequent roofing risk in Kansas.

Class 4 is the highest impact-resistance classification under UL 2218 testing. It does not mean a shingle is hail-proof, but it does indicate that the product has passed a higher level of impact testing than standard roofing materials.

Class 4 shingles may make sense if:

  • Your home has experienced repeated hail exposure
  • You want greater impact resistance
  • You plan to stay in the home long-term
  • You are already replacing the roof and comparing upgrades
  • Your insurance carrier offers discounts for qualifying products

Insurance discounts vary by carrier and policy, so confirm eligibility before choosing a roofing product based on potential savings.

What Warranty Comes With a New Roof?

Learn more about Rhoden Roofing’s Lifetime Warranty.

  5. Installation: Underlayment, flashing, ventilation, roofing materials, and accessories are installed as part of the new system.
  6. Cleanup and final review: The property is cleaned and applicable warranty documentation is provided.

Clear process. Real warranties. No guesswork.

Cost depends on roof size, pitch, material, tear-off, decking condition, ventilation, flashing, access, and warranty options. An inspection is the best way to create an accurate estimate.

Are Class 4 shingles hail-proof?

No. Class 4 shingles are impact-resistant, not hail-proof. Severe hail can still damage roofing materials.

Can Class 4 shingles lower my insurance?

Some carriers may offer discounts for qualifying impact-resistant roofing, but availability and requirements vary.

A small roofing problem can stay small when it is caught early. Leave it alone, and one loose shingle, failed flashing detail, or hidden leak can turn into damaged decking, insulation, ceilings, and a much more expensive project.

Rhoden Roofing LLC provides professional roof repair in Wichita, KS for homeowners dealing with leaks, hail damage, wind damage, missing shingles, flashing problems, and other roofing concerns. What Types of Roof Damage Can Be Repaired?

Not every roofing issue requires a full replacement. Many problems can be corrected with a targeted repair when the surrounding roof is still in good condition.

Common roof damage we repair includes:

  • Missing or wind-lifted shingles
  • Cracked, broken, or damaged shingles
  • Hail-related damage
  • Leaks around vents, chimneys, and roof penetrations
  • Damaged or loose flashing
  • Pipe boot failures
  • Ridge and hip damage
  • Minor decking concerns
  • Storm-damaged roof accessories
  • Water intrusion around valleys or transitions
  • Small areas of material failure
  • Damage caused by fallen limbs or debris

The important part is finding the actual source.

A ceiling stain does not always appear directly below the leak. Water can travel along decking, rafters, fasteners, and insulation before becoming visible inside the home. That is why surface-level patching often fails.

A proper roof repair starts with diagnosis, not caulk.

How Wichita Weather Causes Roof Damage

Wichita roofs deal with more than normal aging. Hail can bruise shingles and knock away protective granules, strong winds can lift roofing materials and loosen flashing, and repeated heat, UV exposure, freezing temperatures, and rapid temperature swings can wear down seals and roofing components over time.

Some of that damage is obvious. Some is not. A roof may look fine from the driveway while still having loosened shingles, damaged flashing, or storm-related wear that can allow water in later.

If your home has recently been through hail, high winds, or severe weather, a professional inspection can help determine whether the damage is limited enough for repair or part of a larger roofing issue.

Should You Repair or Replace Your Roof?

Roof repair makes the most sense when the problem is isolated and the rest of the roofing system still has useful life.

A repair may be appropriate when:

  • Damage affects a small area
  • Matching materials are available
  • The decking remains sound
  • The roof has not developed recurring leaks
  • The surrounding shingles are still flexible and serviceable

Roof replacement may be the better decision when:

  • Leaks keep returning
  • Damage affects multiple slopes
  • The roof is approaching the end of its expected life
  • Shingles are brittle or badly worn
  • Materials can no longer be matched
  • Previous repairs are failing
  • Decking damage is widespread

We do not believe homeowners should be pushed into a new roof when a responsible repair will solve the problem.

We also will not recommend another patch when the roof is clearly telling us it needs more.

What Happens During a Professional Roof Repair?

Finding the Source of the Problem

Reviewing Your Repair Options

We explain what is damaged, whether repair is reasonable, and whether anything else needs attention.

Building the Roof Repair Scope

The recommended work is based on the actual problem rather than a generic repair package.

Completing the Repair With In-House Crews

Rhoden Roofing uses trained in-house crews rather than handing your home to unknown subcontractors. That gives us greater control over workmanship, communication, and project standards.

Standing Behind the Work

Accountability does not stop when the truck leaves. Our warranty philosophy is built around long-term responsibility for the work we perform.

Clear process. Real accountability. No guesswork.

Why You Should Repair Roof Damage Before It Gets Worse

A roof repair is usually less expensive when the damage has not spread.

A small flashing failure can eventually affect roof decking. A missing shingle can expose the underlayment. Water entering through one vulnerable area can damage insulation, drywall, paint, and interior finishes.

Early repair can help:

  • Limit water intrusion
  • Reduce the chance of decking damage
  • Protect insulation and interior finishes
  • Extend the useful life of the roof
  • Reduce repeated emergency repairs
  • Give you time to plan for future replacement

The goal is not to repair a roof forever. It is to get the most reasonable service life from the system without allowing manageable problems to become expensive ones.

Rhoden Roofing has served Kansas property owners since 2008 with a focus on accurate inspections, dependable workmanship, and long-term accountability.

Our trained in-house crews give us greater control over quality and communication, while credentials including GAF Master Elite, Malarkey Emerald Premium Contractor, DaVinci, Ludowici, and a BBB A+ rating reinforce the standards behind the work.

When a New Roof Installation Makes Sense

Residential Roofing Systems We Install in Wichita

Rhoden Roofing installs several residential roofing systems for Wichita homes. Each material has its own strengths, cost range, maintenance needs, and installation requirements.

Asphalt Shingle Roof Installation

Asphalt shingles are one of the most common choices for Wichita homes because they balance cost, durability, style options, and repairability. They work well on many roof designs and can fit both older homes and newer construction.

Rhoden Roofing installs asphalt shingle systems with the details that affect performance, including underlayment, starter shingles, flashing, ridge caps, ventilation, and fastening. Metal Roof Installation

Metal roofing can be a good choice for homeowners who want long-term durability, strong weather performance, and lower maintenance. It can work well on certain homes, garages, porches, and detached structures when the design and budget fit.

Proper installation matters with metal roofing. Fastening, flashing, expansion, roof transitions, and ventilation all need to be handled correctly so the system performs as intended.

Cedar Roof Installation

Cedar roofing adds natural character and a distinct finish to homes where the style fits. It can be a strong option for homeowners who want warmth, texture, and a more traditional look.

Cedar also comes with maintenance expectations. Rhoden Roofing helps homeowners decide whether cedar is a practical fit for the home, neighborhood, and Kansas weather exposure.

Tile Roof Installation

Tile roofs, often made from clay or concrete, are known for durability, low maintenance, and long service life. They can provide a premium look and strong weather resistance when installed on a home that can properly support the system.

Before recommending tile, Rhoden Roofing considers roof structure, weight, slope, flashing needs, and installation requirements.

Slate Roof Installation

Because slate is a specialty roofing system, it requires experienced installers and careful planning. Rhoden Roofing helps homeowners understand whether slate fits the home’s structure, style, and budget.

Low-slope residential roof installation requires the right material, drainage planning, flashing, and seam details. Rhoden Roofing can evaluate the roof area and recommend a system that fits the structure and intended use.

What Proper Roof Installation Includes

A dependable roof starts with the details beneath the surface. Before shingles, panels, or tile go on, the roof needs proper preparation for the home, the material, and the Kansas weather.

Proper residential roof installation Wichita homeowners can trust may include:

  • Checking the roof deck for soft spots, rot, or damaged sheathing.
  • Using underlayment that fits the roof slope and material.
  • Installing ice and water protection where needed.
  • Flashing chimneys, valleys, vents, walls, and roof transitions correctly.
  • Installing starter shingles, ridge caps, drip edge, and roof edges.
  • Using the right fastening pattern for the selected material.
  • Reviewing ventilation and drainage before the roof is finished.
  • Protecting the property, cleaning up, and completing a final review.

These details matter in Wichita. Wind, rain, heat, and attic moisture can expose weak installation, which is why choosing professional roof installers in Wichita, KS, is important.

Types of Metal Roofing

Aluminium Roofing

Aluminium roofing has many benefits that homeowners and business owners are attracted to. Steel Roofing

A popular choice for roofing in hail-prone areas particularly, steel roofing is super durable and low maintenance, which ranks it high on the longevity scale. Like most metal roofing materials, the heat reflection also contributes to reduced energy use and costs.

Copper Roofing

Given its light weight and malleability, it can be fashioned in a variety of ways to mimic tiles, shingles, brick, etc.

Standing Seam Metal Roofing

Standing-seam roofs is the most popular iteration of metal roofing. Essentially, this type of roofing raises the seams beyond the level of the actual roof, thereby creating panels that run from the ridge to the eaves of the roof. Its interlocking system ensures that a watertight seal is created, and also makes it one of the strongest, most reliable roof systems on the market today.

Corrugated Metal Roofing

Its major appeal is the combination of all the great characteristics of metal, while giving homeowners the ability to customize the look and feel to their preference. Metal shingles can mimic the finish of more premium roofing alternatives like slate roofs, clay and concrete tiles and cedar, at a fraction of the cost, and with strength, durability and longevity guaranteed.

Flat Roof Coating

GET A FREE ESTIMATE

Flat Roof Coating Services

Many businesses, commercial buildings, and Rhoden Roofing warehouses have flat roofs. They’re particularly useful for creating extra outdoor space, giving you easy access to clean or repair them, and offer wind resistance.

A common myth is the flat roofs are not durable and cannot hold the weight of snow, but this is not true. Building codes require that flat roofs be able to carry enough weight to protect the structural integrity of the building.

However, what you will find is that flat roofs need a higher degree of maintenance. With that in mind, here are some of the best flat roof coating solutions to protect your roof from the elements and natural aging.

Get A FREE Estimate

Why Apply a Coating?

Flat roof coating can ensure that your roof lasts another 10-15 years without needing to be replaced. It prevents leaks, is easy to apply, and gives you the longevity you need at a much lower cost than replacing the entire roof.

A reliable roof coating company like Rhoden Roofing can inspect your current roof and suggest the best coating for you. Which coating you need depends on the type of roof you have and whether your roof has a high amount of traffic. There are many different solutions you can choose from, so keep reading to see your options.

Types of Flat Roof Coating

There are several types of roof coatings that provide particular benefits to flat roofs. They include asphalt, acrylic, polyureas, and urethanes. Each has a different purpose, so while they all work, your needs will determine which type of flat roof coating you choose.

ASPHALT

Asphalt coatings are mixed with a solvent that helps thin the asphalt, making application easy via spray nozzle or brush. Some asphalt coatings have added aluminum to aid in sun reflection. Other additives can increase the strength, thickness, or longevity of the coating.

Asphalt emulsions use water instead of a solvent to thin the mixture. The same additives can create additional strength, thickness, and longevity, and it’s applied the same way. The benefit of using water is that the solution doesn’t allow water to pool, which can aid in a non-slip surface that can accommodate heavy traffic.

ACRYLIC

Acrylic elastomers are highly reflective and usually installed on bituminous and non-bituminous roofing. This reflective surface aids in deflecting heat, keeping your building cooler and better insulated.

Acrylic is extremely durable. It has been used for decades for Rhoden Roofing purposes, and because of its easy application, it is more cost-effective and provides the best value.

POLYUREAS

Polyureas haven’t been used for as long as some of the other coatings on the market. Some polyureas are similar to polyurethane and others are closer to urethane. These types of coatings are continually being modified by manufacturers to make them even better.

Polyureas provide excellent abrasion resistance, structural enhancement, corrosion protection, waterproofing, and chemical resistance.

URETHANES

Urethanes are used commonly on concrete surfaces like driveways and parking garages. They can also be used on wood. They are used alone and not layered with other roofing products. Urethane coatings are perfect for high traffic areas because they are seamless, flexible, and durable.

Urethane coatings expand and contract with your roof, resist water pooling, and are more impact resistant than many other flat roof coatings.

How Flat Roof Coating is Applied

Flat roof coating contractors usually brush or spray your roof coating onto the surface. The length of the process depends on which kind of coating you choose and the size of your roof.

First, they’ll clean your roof, identifying any areas that need to be repaired. Next, they’ll fix any holes, tears, or open seams so that the coating will be as effective as possible. Then they’ll start in one corner and either spray or brush the coating on in small sections.

The weather conditions have to be just right as well. Applying a roof coating when the roof is too hot or too cold can affect its adhesive qualities. Sometimes a flat roof coating service will only work early in the morning if the peak temperatures that day are not favorable.

It can take up to 24 hours for the coating to dry and your flat roof coating company may recommend you stay off it for even longer depending on how much time it needs to set.

Types of Corrugated Metal

U-Panel

U-panel sheets have 26-gauge panels and are the most common choice for homes because they’re the most visually appealing. Installation is easy and more affordable because the existing roof does not need to be removed. The roof can thus be placed on top of an existing roof.

R-Panel

R-panel corrugated sheets are more durable and require less maintenance than other types of corrugated metal roofing materials. They last longer and are typically used more frequently on commercial buildings because they have a more rugged design.

Corrugated metal roofs enable water runoff and are surprisingly quiet during a storm. A common misconception is that all metal roofs are loud, but if properly installed and insulated, this doesn’t need to be the case.

Galvanized steel already has excessive strength, but the corrugation process enhances this strength since the corrugation runs perpendicular to the grooves in the steel. It can last up to one hundred years if properly installed and maintained. Because steel and aluminum don’t rust or fade, it will look just as new as the day you had it installed. It’s also not vulnerable to termites, contributing to its longevity.

Weather Resistance
